definition_zh: 合伙；伙伴关系；合伙企业；（体育）搭档关系
definition_en: a business or working relationship between partners, or the state of being partners in an activity
core_image: 两人共用一张工作台，任何一个抽屉都能被其中任何一人拉开
scene: 店门口的木牌上刻着两个姓氏，中间没有分隔符。 The two firms formed a partnership to bid for the bridge contract.
sceneCN: 这里 partnership 指「两个主体共同出资、共同承担的合作关系」（第 1 个义项：商业上的合伙）；句意为两家公司组成合伙关系，以投标这项桥梁工程。可辨识物件：木牌、两个姓氏、投标文件、模型桥；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 合伙；合伙企业；伙伴关系

senses.title: A firm owned by partners
senses.definition: a business in which two or more people share ownership, profits and liability
senses.definitionCN: 由两人或更多人共同拥有、共享利润并共担责任的企业
senses.example: The two firms formed a partnership to bid for the bridge contract.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司组成合伙关系，以投标这项桥梁工程。
senses.why: the noun ending -ship marks a state or a body, so partner plus -ship can name the firm itself.
senses.whyCN: 名词词尾 -ship 标记一种状态或一个团体，因此 partner 加 -ship 可以直接命名这家企业。

senses.title: The relationship of partners
senses.definition: the working relation between people who share an enterprise
senses.definitionCN: 共同经营一项事业的人之间的工作关系
senses.example: Their partnership survived two failed ventures.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的合伙关系在两次失败的项目之后仍然存续。
senses.why: the same ending can name the bond rather than the body, which is why the word covers both.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词尾既可以命名「关系」，也可以命名「团体」，因此这个词同时覆盖两者。

senses.title: Cooperation between organizations
senses.definition: a formal working arrangement between bodies that remain separate
senses.definitionCN: 各自独立的两方之间正式的工作安排
senses.example: The city entered a partnership with the railway company.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府与铁路公司建立了合作关系。
senses.why: modern usage loosened the legal core: two bodies can be partners without merging.
senses.whyCN: 现代用法松开了法律内核：两个机构不必合并也可以称伙伴。

senses.title: Two batters at one wicket
senses.titleCN: 板球中同时在场的一对击球手
senses.definition: in cricket, the pair batting together and the runs they add
senses.definitionCN: 板球中同时在场的两名击球手，以及他们共同取得的分数
senses.example: Their opening partnership added ninety runs.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的开局搭档贡献了九十分。
senses.why: sport borrows the word for any pair that must cover for each other on the field.
senses.whyCN: 体育借这个词指任何在场上必须替对方补位的一对。

senses.title: A pairing at the card table
senses.definition: in card games, the pair who play as a team against other pairs
senses.definitionCN: 牌戏中作为一队对抗其他各对的两个人
senses.example: They have been a partnership at bridge for thirty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在桥牌上做搭档已经三十年。
senses.why: a card pair must trust the other's unseen hand, which is partnership in its purest social form.
senses.whyCN: 一对牌手必须信赖对方看不见的牌，这是「合伙」最纯粹的社会形态。

senses.title: Shared responsibility in policy
senses.definition: an arrangement in which government, employers and workers share duties
senses.definitionCN: 政府、雇主与劳动者分担责任的一种安排
senses.example: The wage deal rested on a social partnership.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工资协议建立在社会伙伴关系之上。
senses.why: politics uses the word for duties shared across sectors, where no contract binds the parties.
senses.whyCN: 政治用这个词指跨部门分担的责任，那里并没有合同约束各方。

senses.title: A legally recognised couple
senses.definition: a civil partnership giving a couple rights similar to marriage
senses.definitionCN: 给予一对伴侣类似婚姻权利的民事伴侣关系
senses.example: The law allowed a civil partnership from that year.
senses.exampleCN: 从那一年起，法律允许登记民事伴侣关系。
senses.why: the word spread from commerce to domestic life because both rest on a formal sharing of assets and duties.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从商业扩展到家庭生活，因为两者都建立在正式共享财产与责任之上。

senses.title: A coalition of parties
senses.definition: a governing arrangement between political parties that share power
senses.definitionCN: 分享权力的政党之间的执政安排
senses.example: The coalition called itself a partnership of equals.
senses.exampleCN: 这个联合政府自称是平等者之间的伙伴关系。
senses.why: coalitions borrow the commercial word to sound voluntary, since no party was bought.
senses.whyCN: 联合政府借用商业词，是为了听起来出于自愿，因为并没有哪一党被买下。

intro.en: Partnership is partner plus -ship, an Old English ending for a state or a body. Partner came from Old French parçonier, a sharer, from Latin partitio 'a division'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: partnership 是 partner 加 -ship 构成，后者是古英语中表示状态或团体的词尾。partner 来自古法语 parçonier「分有者」，源头是拉丁 partitio「分割」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pars meant 'a part, a share'. From it come partition, particle and the whole family of English part words.
items.cn: pars 意为「一部分、一份」。partition、particle 以及英语中整个 part 词族都由此而来。

items.en: Partitio, from partire 'to divide', named a dividing or a share, and Old French turned it into parçon.
items.cn: partitio 出自 partire「分割」，命名分割或所分得的一份，古法语把它变成 parçon。

items.en: Parçonier meant 'a sharer, one who has a part', and English borrowed it as partner in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: parçonier 意为「分有者、占一份的人」，英语在十三世纪以 partner 的形式借入。

items.en: The Old English ending -scipe marked state or condition, as in friendship and lordship; added to partner it made partnership around 1400.
items.cn: 古英语词尾 -scipe 标记状态或情形，如 friendship 与 lordship；加在 partner 上，约在十五世纪初形成 partnership。

items.en: From the eighteenth century the word hardened into a legal form of business, with deeds, liability and dissolution.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，这个词固化为一种法律上的企业形式，有了契约、责任与解散程序。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact first citation of partnership varies between dictionaries, and the pre-Latin history of pars is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各家词典对 partnership 最早的用例说法不一；pars 在拉丁语之前的历史属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words on the same part root or on confusing near-forms; group two holds nouns for people or bodies that work as one.
note.cn: 第一组收同出「部分」词根、或形近易混的词；第二组收表示「作为一体运作的人或团体」的名词。

entries.definition: From Latin partitio: a division or a dividing screen, which is the physical act of what partnership shares.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 partitio：分割或隔板，正是 partnership 所「分有」的那个动作本身。

entries.definition: From Italian parte, a faction: a committed supporter of one side, sharing the root but not the mutual duty.
entries.definitionCN: 来自意大利语 parte「派别」：某一方的坚定支持者，同根，却不含相互的责任。

entries.definition: A sharer in an enterprise; partnership is the state or the body formed by such sharers.
entries.definitionCN: 共同经营中的分有者；partnership 则是由这些分有者形成的状态或团体。

entries.definition: A rarer form with co-, used mostly in older commercial writing for the same arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 加 co- 的较罕形式，多见于较早的商业文书，指同一种安排。

entries.definition: A union of separate parties for a purpose; it stresses remaining separate more than sharing ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 为某种目的把各自独立的两方联合起来；更强调「仍然分开」，而非共享所有权。

entries.definition: A single business project shared by two firms; a partnership may run many projects over years.
entries.definitionCN: 两家公司共担的单一商业项目；而 partnership 可能持续多年、涵盖多个项目。

entries.definition: A separate legal entity; partners are personally liable, which a company's owners are not.
entries.definitionCN: 独立的法律实体；合伙人承担个人责任，而公司的所有者不承担。

entries.definition: A group of people organized around a shared interest; it need not trade or share profit.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕共同兴趣组织起来的一群人；它不必经商，也不必分利。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Partner plus -ship, the ending that turns a person into a state or a body.
normal.cn: partner 加 -ship，后者把一个人变成一种状态或一个团体。

normal.en: The family runs partner, partnership, partnering, partnered, copartnership.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 partner、partnership、partnering、partnered、copartnership。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the stages: enter into partnership, dissolve a partnership.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出阶段：结成合伙、解散合伙。

normal.en: The partner root means a share, so a partnership is literally a sharing.
normal.cn: partner 的词根意为「一份」，所以 partnership 字面上就是「分有」。

normal.en: Sport and cards keep older senses alive: a batting partnership, a bridge partnership.
normal.cn: 体育与牌戏让较早的义项存活：击球搭档、桥牌搭档。

abstract.cn: 想象一块木牌上刻着两个姓氏，中间没有分隔符。

abstract.en: Picture one drawer that either of two people can open.
abstract.cn: 想象一只抽屉，两个人里任何一个都能拉开。

abstract.en: Picture a boat rowed by two oars that must enter the water together.
abstract.cn: 想象一条船由两支桨划动，两支桨必须同时入水。

examples.en: The partnership was dissolved after the senior partner retired.
examples.cn: 资深合伙人退休后，这份合伙关系解散了。

examples.en: The museum works in partnership with three local schools.
examples.cn: 博物馆与三所本地学校合作。

examples.en: Their partnership at the card table lasted longer than their marriage.
examples.cn: 他们在牌桌上的搭档关系，比他们的婚姻还长久。

root: partner（古法语 parçonier「分有者」，源自拉丁 pars「部分」、partitio「分割」）+ -ship（古英语 -scipe，表状态或团体），约十五世纪初成词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all describe people who hold parts of one thing together: a firm, a bond, two organizations, a batting pair, a card pair, a policy deal, a legal couple and a coalition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都描述「共同持有一件事的各一份」的人：一家企业、一段关系、两个机构、一对击球手、一对牌手、一份政策约定、一对法律伴侣，以及一个联合政府。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one workbench shared by two people, with every drawer open to either of them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人共用一张工作台，每只抽屉对两人都敞开。

branches.en: THE FIRM AND THE BOND: the body that owns, and the relation that holds it together.
branches.cn: 企业与其纽带：拥有它的团体，以及把它维系住的关系。

branches.en: ORGANIZATIONS AND POLICY: bodies cooperate, and government shares duties with industry.
branches.cn: 机构与政策：机构之间合作，政府与产业分担责任。

branches.en: THE FIELD AND THE TABLE: a batting pair and a card pair, where trust is physical.
branches.cn: 球场与牌桌：一对击球手与一对牌手，信任在那里是身体性的。

branches.en: A LEGAL COUPLE: the commercial word enters domestic law.
branches.cn: 法律上的伴侣：商业词进入了家庭法。

branches.en: A COALITION: parties call their power-sharing a partnership of equals.
branches.cn: 联合政府：各党把自己的分权安排称作平等者之间的伙伴关系。

intro.en: Partnership combines a French noun of sharing with an Old English ending for a state, which is why it can name both a firm and a relation.
intro.cn: partnership 把一个法语「分有」名词与一个古英语「状态」词尾合在一起，因此它既能命名企业，也能命名关系。

latinIntro.en: Latin pars 'part' yields part, partition and particle, and the French derivative parçonier gives English partner.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pars「部分」衍生 part、partition 与 particle，其法语派生词 parçonier 给出英语的 partner。

definition_en: a person who cuts up and sells meat

scene: 市场尽头的铺子挂着整扇肉。 The butcher sharpened his knife behind the counter.

derivatives.zh: 屠宰，与 butcher 的动作相近

senses.title: A person who sells meat
senses.definition: a person who cuts up meat and sells it
senses.definitionCN: 切割并出售肉类的人
senses.example: The butcher sharpened his knife behind the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 肉贩在柜台后磨刀。
senses.why: This is the main sense, from a word for one who kills goats.
senses.whyCN: 这是主要义项，源自「宰羊的人」。

senses.title: To kill and cut up animals
senses.definition: to kill animals and cut them into meat
senses.definitionCN: 宰杀牲畜并切成肉块
senses.example: They butchered a pig for the feast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为宴席宰了一头猪。
senses.why: The trade gave its name to the work it does.
senses.whyCN: 这个行当把名字给了它所做的活。

senses.title: To spoil something badly
senses.definition: to do something so badly that it is ruined
senses.definitionCN: 把事情做得极糟，弄坏了
senses.example: He butchered the song at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 他在聚会上把那首歌唱得一塌糊涂。
senses.why: Cutting a thing carelessly ruins it, like meat cut wrong.
senses.whyCN: 乱切会把东西毁掉，就像肉被切坏了。

definition_zh: 怪异的；怪诞的；不寻常的；神秘而可怕的
definition_en: strange, unusual, or uncanny in a way that is hard to explain
core_image: 午夜里一件本该正常却微微走形的东西
scene: 旧宅的走廊尽头，挂钟在毫无风的时候自己摆动。 A weird feeling came over her as the clock moved by itself.
sceneCN: 这里 weird 是「怪异而神秘的」（第 1 个义项：反常到难以解释）；句意是看到挂钟自己摆动，她涌起一种说不出的怪异感。

derivatives.zh: weird + -ly，义为「怪异地；不可思议地」
weird + -o 口语后缀，义为「怪人」（带贬义）

senses.title: Strange and hard to explain
senses.definition: very strange and difficult to explain or understand
senses.definitionCN: 非常奇怪，难以解释或理解
senses.example: A weird light flickered in the empty hallway.
senses.exampleCN: 空荡的走廊里闪过一道怪异的光。
senses.why: The core image is something slightly wrong with the normal world, beyond a ready explanation.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是正常世界出现了说不清道不明的偏差，超出随手可得的解释。

senses.title: Uncanny or supernatural
senses.titleCN: 神秘而可怕的；有超自然色彩的
senses.definition: connected with fate or the supernatural, suggesting uncanny power
senses.definitionCN: 与命运或超自然相关，透着诡异的气息
senses.example: They met at midnight among the weird standing stones.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜时分，他们在那些诡异的立石间相会。
senses.why: This is the older sense preserved: the weird sisters of legend told fortunes, so weird keeps a taste of fate.
senses.whyCN: 这是保留下来的古义：传说中的「命运三姐妹」操持预言，weird 因此带着命运的余味。

senses.title: Unusual in an interesting way
senses.titleCN: 别致的；出人意表的新奇
senses.definition: unusual but attractive or interesting, often said of art or style
senses.definitionCN: 与众不同但有趣、有吸引力，常用于形容艺术或风格
senses.example: The gallery shows weird and wonderful sculptures.
senses.exampleCN: 这家画廊展出光怪陆离又妙趣横生的雕塑。
senses.why: Departure from the normal is not always frightening; it can delight, so weird turns positive in taste contexts.
senses.whyCN: 偏离常规未必可怕，也可能令人愉悦，于是在品味语境中 weird 转为褒义。

senses.title: Behaving strangely as a person
senses.definition: describing a person whose behavior others find odd
senses.definitionCN: 形容人的言行让他人觉得古怪
senses.example: He is a bit weird, but everyone likes him.
senses.exampleCN: 他有点古怪，但大家都喜欢他。
senses.why: A style or habit that breaks norms is read first as strangeness in the person.
senses.whyCN: 打破常规的作风或习惯，首先被解读为此人身上的「怪」。

senses.title: Feeling strange or unwell
senses.titleCN: 感觉不对劲的；不自在的
senses.definition: feeling odd, uncomfortable, or not normal, about the body or mood
senses.definitionCN: 身体或情绪感觉异常、不自在
senses.example: The medicine made her feel weird all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 那种药让她整个下午都感觉不对劲。
senses.why: When the self departs from its own normal, the same word for a strange world covers a strange feeling.
senses.whyCN: 当自我偏离了自身的常态，形容世界之怪的那个词便也覆盖了感觉之怪。

senses.title: Remarkably coincidental
senses.definition: so coincidental that it seems planned or uncanny
senses.definitionCN: 巧合到仿佛冥冥中安排好的地步
senses.example: It was weird that we both booked the same seat.
senses.exampleCN: 我们俩订了同一个座位，真是巧得出奇。
senses.why: Coincidence beyond chance feels like fate, linking back to the old sense of destiny.
senses.whyCN: 超出概率的巧合让人感到命运之手，正好接回古老的「命运」义。

senses.title: Weird weather or atmosphere
senses.definition: abnormal, said of weather, atmosphere, or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 形容天气、氛围或状况反常
senses.example: Weird weather hit the coast this winter.
senses.exampleCN: 今年冬天海岸边出现了反常天气。
senses.why: Nature off its usual rhythm produces the same unexplainable wrongness.
senses.whyCN: 自然偏离惯常节律时，同样呈现出那种说不清的反常。

senses.title: Weird as deliberate oddity
senses.definition: intentionally strange in design or performance
senses.definitionCN: 在设计或表演上故意追求怪诞
senses.example: The band is famous for its weird stage costumes.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队以刻意怪诞的舞台服装著称。
senses.why: Artists seize the uncanny on purpose, making strangeness a signature.
senses.whyCN: 创作者刻意抓取诡异感，把「怪」变成个人标志。

intro.en: Weird began as a noun of fate in Old English and shifted into today's adjective of strangeness.
intro.cn: weird 最初是古英语中的「命运」名词，后来才转变为今天表示「怪异」的形容词。

items.en: The root *wert- meant to turn, generally reconstructed as the source of the fate word.
items.cn: 一般认为其源头是意为「转动」的词根 *wert-，「命运」即「转动中落到身上之物」。

items.en: The form *wurthis meant that which turns, hence one's lot or destiny.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 *wurthis 意为「转动之物」，引申为人的际遇或命运。

items.en: Old English wyrd meant fate or destiny, a person's appointed lot.
items.cn: 古英语 wyrd 意为「命运、定数」，指人被安排的际遇。

items.en: The noun survived in the weird sisters, the fate-spinning figures of legend and literature.
items.cn: 名词保留在传说中的「命运三姐妹」（weird sisters）里，即纺织命运的女巫形象。

items.en: From the fate-women came the adjective weird meaning uncanny or fateful, popularized by Shakespeare's witches.
items.cn: 由命运女巫生出形容词 weird「诡异、应验般的」，经莎士比亚笔下的女巫而流行。

items.en: The fate meaning faded and weird settled as the everyday word for strange and unexplainable.
items.cn: 「命运」义渐弱，weird 定型为日常表示「奇怪、难以解释」的词。

note.en: Weird is close to strange but adds an uncanny edge, and its spelling history links it to fate words.
note.cn: weird 与 strange 相近但更带一丝诡异，其拼写史又把它与「命运」一词相系。

entries.definition: in a strange or uncanny way
entries.definitionCN: 怪异地；不可思议地。weird 的副词

entries.definitionCN: 古英语「命运」，weird 的直接前身

root: weird 源自古英语名词 wyrd「命运」，可追溯至原始日耳曼语 *wurthis「转动之物」（一般认为源自原始印欧语词根 *wert-「转动」），即「转落到人身上的际遇」。中古英语保留于 the weird sisters（命运三姐妹），十六世纪由「命运的」转为「诡异的」，最终定型为「怪异的」形容词。

sensesIntro.en: From its fate-spinning past, weird moves through uncanny strangeness, delightful oddity, odd people, odd feelings, strange coincidence, freak weather, and deliberate eccentricity.
sensesIntro.cn: 从纺织命运的过往出发，weird 依次经过诡异难解、新奇可喜、古怪之人、异常之感、离奇巧合、反常天气与刻意怪诞。

senses.title: A serious disagreement
senses.definition: a long or serious disagreement between people, groups or countries
senses.definitionCN: 个人、团体或国家之间长时间或严重的分歧
senses.example: The conflict lasted for many years.
senses.exampleCN: 这场冲突持续了许多年。
senses.why: Two sides want opposite things, and neither will step back.
senses.whyCN: 双方想要相反的东西，谁都不肯退让。

senses.title: A clash between ideas or rules
senses.definition: a situation where two ideas, rules or duties cannot both be true
senses.definitionCN: 两种想法、规则或职责无法同时成立的情形
senses.example: There is a conflict between the two rules.

items.en: Fligere meant to strike or knock something down.

items.en: Confligere meant to strike two forces against each other.

items.en: Conflictus named the clash itself.
items.cn: conflictus 指撞击这件事本身。

items.en: French conflit carried the sense into disputes between people.
items.cn: 法语 conflit 把这个意思带入人与人之间的争端。

items.en: English conflict now covers war, argument and contradiction alike.
items.cn: 英语 conflict 如今同时覆盖战争、争吵与自相矛盾。

normal.en: When words conflict with actions, believe the actions.

definition_zh: 百分比；百分率；占比；按比例的分成；百分点；（口语）好处
definition_en: a rate or share expressed per hundred; also a proportion of a whole, a commission, and informally, an advantage
core_image: 一条被切成一百格的长条，其中若干格被涂上颜色
scene: 教室墙上贴着一条一百格的长条，三十格涂成橙色。 The teacher pointed at the coloured squares and said that thirty out of one hundred was the percentage she wanted them to remember.
sceneCN: 这里 percentage 是「百分比」（第 1 个义项：以百为基数的比率）；句意：老师指着涂色的格子说，一百格里的三十格就是她要学生记住的百分比。图中可辨识物件：一百格长条、橙色涂格、白色空格、教鞭、数字标签；对应第 1 个义项。

derivatives.zh: 百分点（两个百分比之间的差）
每百；百分之（英式分写形式）

senses.title: A rate per hundred
senses.definition: a number or rate expressed as a fraction of one hundred
senses.definitionCN: 以一百为分母表示的数值或比率
senses.example: Write the answer as a percentage rather than a decimal.
senses.exampleCN: 把答案写成百分比，而不是小数。
senses.why: Percent is Latin per centum, 'by the hundred'. The -age suffix turns that phrase into a noun of rate, so a percentage is literally the result of counting how many parts there are in every hundred.
senses.whyCN: percent 是拉丁语 per centum，“每一百”。-age 后缀把这个短语变成表示比率的名词，因此 percentage 字面上就是“每一百里有多少份”的计数结果。

senses.title: The share of a whole
senses.definition: a proportion of a total, expressed or understood as a rate out of a hundred
senses.definitionCN: 总量中的一份，以百为基数表示或理解
senses.example: A large percentage of the students live on campus.
senses.exampleCN: 很大比例的学生住在校内。
senses.why: Once the hundred-part strip is drawn, any whole can be mapped onto it. The percentage becomes a way of comparing shares from different totals, which is why it is the standard language of surveys.
senses.whyCN: 一百格长条一旦画好，任何整体都能映射上去。百分比于是成为比较不同总量中份额的方式，因此它成了调查的标准语言。

senses.title: A rate of change
senses.definition: a figure expressing how much something has increased or decreased relative to its earlier level
senses.definitionCN: 表示某物相对先前水平增加或减少多少的数值
senses.example: Sales fell by a small percentage last quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 上季度销售额小幅下降。
senses.why: A change can be measured against the old total, and the old total can be treated as one hundred. The percentage then describes the movement rather than the thing moved.
senses.whyCN: 变化可以对照旧总量来量，而旧总量可以被当作一百。于是百分比描述的是“移动了多少”，而不是被移动的那个东西。

senses.title: A percentage point
senses.definition: one unit of difference between two percentages, as opposed to a relative change
senses.definitionCN: 两个百分比之间相差的一个单位，区别于相对变化
senses.example: The rate moved from ten to twelve percent, a rise of two percentage points.
senses.exampleCN: 比率从百分之十升到百分之十二，上升了两个百分点。
senses.why: A change from ten to twelve percent is a fifth in relative terms but only two units on the hundred-grid. English keeps the grid unit separate with the phrase percentage point, precisely to stop the two readings from being confused.
senses.whyCN: 从百分之十到百分之十二，相对变化是五分之一，但在百格图上只移动了两格。英语用 percentage point 单独命名这个格子单位，正是为了不让两种读法混淆。

senses.title: A commission: a percentage of the deal
senses.titleCN: 佣金：交易额的一个百分比
senses.definition: a share of a sale or profit paid to an agent, calculated as a rate per hundred
senses.definitionCN: 按每百比率计算、支付给代理人的销售额或利润份额
senses.example: The agent takes a percentage of every sale.
senses.exampleCN: 代理人从每笔销售中抽取一定比例的佣金。
senses.why: Commerce needed a neutral way to divide a deal without naming a fixed sum. A percentage lets the payment scale with the sale, so the rate itself becomes the agreement.
senses.whyCN: 商业需要一种中立方式来分配交易，而不必写死一个金额。百分比让报酬随销售额缩放，于是“比率”本身就成了协议。

senses.title: A chance, stated per hundred
senses.titleCN: 以百为基数陈述的概率
senses.definition: a probability or likelihood expressed as a rate out of one hundred
senses.definitionCN: 以一百为基数表示的可能性或概率
senses.example: There is only a small percentage chance of rain tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 明天下雨的可能性很小。
senses.why: Probability is already a number between zero and one. Scaling it to a hundred makes it readable without decimals, and the word carries that scaling rather than the underlying mathematics.
senses.whyCN: 概率本来是零到一之间的数。把它放大到一百，就能不用小数直接读懂，而这个词承载的正是这个缩放，而不是底层的数学。

senses.title: The composition of a mixture
senses.definition: the proportion of a component in a substance, alloy, or mixture
senses.definitionCN: 某一成分在物质、合金或混合物中所占的比例
senses.example: The alloy contains a small percentage of nickel.
senses.exampleCN: 这种合金含有少量镍。
senses.why: Recipes and specifications need shares that hold at any batch size. Percentage gives a composition that can be reproduced in a laboratory or a factory without fixing the absolute amounts.
senses.whyCN: 配方与规格需要一种在任何批量下都成立的份额。百分比给出一种可在实验室或工厂复现的成分，而不必固定绝对用量。

senses.title: What is in it for me: no percentage in it
senses.titleCN: 有没有好处：no percentage in it
senses.definition: informally, an advantage or profit to be gained from an action
senses.definitionCN: 口语中，从某项行动中可获得的好处或利益
senses.example: There is no percentage in arguing with him.
senses.exampleCN: 和他争论没有任何好处。
senses.why: If a share can be counted per hundred, it can also be counted for oneself. The slang sense asks what share of the gain comes back to me, and drops the arithmetic while keeping the self-interest.
senses.whyCN: 如果份额可以按百计算，也就可以为自己计算。这一俚语义问的是“收益中有多少回到我这儿”，它丢掉了算术，却保留了私利。

intro.en: Percentage is a modern English noun built on percent, which came from Latin per centum. Its root is centum 'hundred', unrelated to the capere of perceive; only the per- is shared.
intro.cn: percentage 是建立在 percent 之上的现代英语名词，而 percent 来自拉丁语 per centum。其词根是 centum“百”，与 perceive 的 capere 无关；两者只共享 per- 这个前缀。

items.en: Percent and the phrase per cent are recorded, from Italian per cento and Modern Latin per centum, both meaning 'by the hundred'. The expression was used in commercial arithmetic.
items.cn: percent 与短语 per cent 记录于 16 世纪 60 年代，来自意大利语 per cento 与近代拉丁语 per centum，二者都意为“每一百”。这一表达用于商业算术。

items.en: Centum is the Latin word for 'one hundred'. It is generally connected with PIE *dekm- 'ten', through an extended form, though the exact prehistory is source uncertain.
items.cn: centum 是拉丁语“一百”。一般把它通过一个扩展形式连到原始印欧语 *dekm-“十”，但其确切史前过程来源不确定。

items.en: Percentage is formed in English from percent plus the noun suffix -age. It names the rate itself rather than the phrase 'per cent'.
items.cn: percentage 于 1789 年由 percent 加名词后缀 -age 构成。它命名比率本身，而不是 per cent 这个短语。

items.en: The commercial sense 'a commission or allowance calculated as a rate' is recorded. Percentage becomes a standard word in trade and finance.
items.cn: “按比率计算的佣金或酬金”这一商业义记录于 1862 年。percentage 成为贸易与金融中的标准词。

items.en: Statistics and polling make percentage a everyday unit, and percentage point is coined to separate an absolute difference of two rates from a relative change. The slang sense 'advantage' also spreads.
items.cn: 统计学与民调让 percentage 成为日常单位，并造出 percentage point，以区分两个比率的绝对差与相对变化。俚语义“好处”也随之扩散。

note.en: The first group is the percent cluster, where the forms are easy to mix up; the second compares words for shares and rates.
note.cn: 第一组是 percent 词群，几种形式容易混用；第二组比较表示“份额与比率”的词。

entries.definition: the rate itself, as in five percent. It is the number or phrase; percentage is the noun for such a rate in general.
entries.definitionCN: 比率本身，如 five percent。它是数字或短语；percentage 是泛指这类比率的名词。

entries.definition: one unit of absolute difference between two percentages. It prevents a rise from ten to twelve percent being called a two percent rise.
entries.definitionCN: 两个百分比之间绝对差的一个单位。它避免把百分之十到十二说成“上升百分之二”。

entries.definition: a value below which a given percentage of observations fall. It is a position in a distribution, not a share of a total.
entries.definitionCN: 有给定百分比的观测值低于该值。它是分布中的位置，不是整体中的份额。

entries.definition: the British two-word spelling of percent. It is the same phrase, written apart and often used before a noun.
entries.definitionCN: percent 的英式分写形式。同一个短语，分开写，常用于名词前。

entries.definition: a part considered in relation to the whole. It needs no hundred as a base, while percentage always does.
entries.definitionCN: 相对于整体来考虑的一部分。它不必以百为基数，而 percentage 总是以百为基数。

entries.definition: a part given to or held by someone. It is concrete and often possessive, while percentage is a neutral rate.
entries.definitionCN: 分给或由某人持有的一份。它具体、常含归属，而 percentage 是中性的比率。

entries.definition: a measure of one quantity against another. It is the broader category, and a percentage is one kind of rate.
entries.definitionCN: 一个量对另一个量的度量。它是更宽的类别，percentage 是其中一种比率。

entries.definition: a numerical part of a whole, written as one number over another. It is exact and flexible, while a percentage fixes the denominator at one hundred.
entries.definitionCN: 整体的数值部分，写作一个数比另一个数。它精确而灵活，而 percentage 把分母固定为一百。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks on per + cent + age, then three abstract images about the hundred-grid.
normalIntro.cn: 先用五个围绕 per + cent + age 的挂钩，再用三个关于“百格图”的抽象画面。

normal.en: per cent is Latin for 'by the hundred'. Percentage is that phrase turned into a noun.
normal.cn: per cent 是拉丁语“每一百”。percentage 就是把这个短语变成名词。

normal.en: cent means hundred: a century is a hundred years, a cent is a hundredth of a dollar, a percentage is a rate per hundred.
normal.cn: cent 是“百”：一世纪是一百年，一美分是一美元的百分之一，percentage 是每一百的比率。

normal.en: Draw a strip of one hundred squares. Colour thirty. You have just drawn thirty percentage.
normal.cn: 画一条一百格的长条，涂三十格。你刚刚画出了百分之三十。

normal.en: Percentage point is the grid unit; percent change is the relative jump. Two different rulers for the same move.
normal.cn: 百分点是格子单位；百分比变化是相对跳跃。同一次移动，两把不同的尺。

normal.en: No percentage in it means no slice of the gain comes back to you.
normal.cn: no percentage in it 意思是收益里没有一片回到你手上。

abstract.en: A percentage is a machine for comparing unequal wholes: it maps every total onto the same hundred squares.
abstract.cn: 百分比是一台比较不等总量的机器：它把每个总和都映射到同一百格上。

abstract.en: The hundred-grid hides the base. Ten percent of a small thing and ten percent of a large thing look identical on the strip.
abstract.cn: 百格图隐藏了基数。小东西的百分之十与大东西的百分之十，在长条上长得一模一样。

abstract.en: A percentage can describe a share or demand one; the same number is a description in a report and a bill in a contract.
abstract.cn: 百分比可以描述一份，也可以索取一份；同一个数字，在报告里是描述，在合同里是账单。

examples.en: The percentage of households with internet access passed ninety.
examples.cn: 拥有互联网接入的家庭比例超过了百分之九十。

examples.en: Unemployment fell by half a percentage point, which is not the same as falling by half a percent.
examples.cn: 失业率下降了半个百分点，这与下降百分之半不是一回事。

examples.en: The agent works on a percentage rather than a salary.
examples.cn: 这位代理人按比例抽成，而不是拿固定薪水。

dict_mnemonic.note: per 记成“每一”，cent 记成“百”，-age 记成名词：每一百中的多少，就是百分比。
dict_mnemonic.text: per（每一）+ cent（百）+ -age（名词）→ 每一百中的份额 → 百分比、占比、佣金

root: percent（16 世纪 60 年代，来自近代拉丁 per centum“每一百”）+ -age；centum“百”与原始印欧语 *dekm-“十”同源（一般认为）。

sensesIntro.en: The senses start with the hundred-based rate, then the share of any whole, the rate of change, the single grid point, the commission, the stated chance, the composition of a mixture, and the slang advantage of a deal.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从“以百为基数的比率”开始，转到任何整体中的占比、变化的比率、单个格子即百分点、佣金、被陈述的概率、混合物的成分比例，最后落到口语中一笔交易的好处。

core.en: A strip of one hundred squares with some of them coloured in
core.cn: 一条一百格的长条，其中若干格被涂上颜色

chain: WHAT IS IN IT FOR ME

branches.en: The instrument and its use: a rate per hundred, and any whole mapped onto it.
branches.cn: 工具及其用途：每一百的比率，以及被映射上去的任何整体。

branches.en: Movement on the grid: a relative change, and the single point that separates two rates.
branches.cn: 格子上的移动：相对变化，以及把两个比率分开的单个点。

branches.en: The share that comes back: a commission, and the slang gain for oneself.
branches.cn: 回到手中的份额：佣金，以及俚语里为自己算的那份好处。

branches.en: Probability: a chance written per hundred.
branches.cn: 概率：写成每一百的机会。

branches.en: Composition: the recipe of a mixture, expressed on the same hundred-grid.
branches.cn: 成分：混合物的配方，也表达在同一张百格图上。

intro.en: Percentage belongs to the cent- family, which is large and stable: percent, percentage point, percentile, and the older hundred words cent, century, centennial.
intro.cn: percentage 属于 cent- 词族，这个族大而稳定：percent、percentage point、percentile，以及更古老的“百”词 cent、century、centennial。

latinIntro.en: Latin centum 'hundred' gives the stem, and the phrase per centum 'by the hundred' gives percent. The suffix -age is native French-derived English, so the word mixes a Latin base with a Romance noun ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 centum“百”提供词干，短语 per centum“每一百”给出 percent。后缀 -age 是经法语进入英语的，因此这个词把拉丁词基与罗曼语名词词尾混合在一起。

items.meaning: in each hundred; a hundred-based rate
items.meaningCN: 每一百中；以百为基数的比率

items.meaning: a rate or share expressed per hundred
items.meaningCN: 以百表示的比率或份额

items.meaning: one unit of difference between two percentages
items.meaningCN: 两个百分比之间相差的一个单位
items.example: The gap narrowed by one percentage point.
items.exampleCN: 差距缩小了一个百分点。

items.meaning: the value below which a given percentage falls
items.meaningCN: 有给定百分比低于其下的值；百分位数
items.example: She scored in the ninetieth percentile.
items.exampleCN: 她的成绩位于第九十百分位。

items.meaning: the same phrase, written as two words
items.meaningCN: 同一个短语，分写为两个词
items.example: A five per cent rise was announced.
items.exampleCN: 宣布了百分之五的涨幅。

items.meaningCN: 一美元的百分之一；美分

items.meaning: a period of one hundred years

items.exampleCN: 这座桥矗立了一个世纪。

items.example: The town held a centennial parade.
items.exampleCN: 小镇举行了一百周年游行。

items.meaning: a temperature scale of one hundred steps
items.meaningCN: 分为一百度的温标；摄氏
items.example: Water boils at one hundred degrees centigrade.

latinEntries.example: Centum is the base of percent and century.
latinEntries.exampleCN: centum 是 percent 与 century 的词基。

latinEntries.meaning: by the hundred; for each hundred
latinEntries.exampleCN: per centum 变成英语 percent。

latinEntries.meaning: a division of a hundred men; a hundred
latinEntries.example: Centuria is the source of English century.
latinEntries.exampleCN: centuria 是英语 century 的来源。

definition_en: after something else happened
core_image: 前一件事落幕后，镜头切到下一幕
scene: 他随后搬到了另一座城市。 He subsequently moved to another city.
sceneCN: 这里 subsequently 是「随后」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他随后搬到了另一座城市。

senses.title: After that
senses.definition: after something else has happened
senses.definitionCN: 在另一件事发生之后

senses.why: This is the basic time sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的时间义项。

senses.title: Later on
senses.definition: at a later time, often in a report or story
senses.definitionCN: 在较晚的时候，常用于报告或叙述
senses.example: The study was subsequently published.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究后来发表了。
senses.why: Formal writing uses it to mark a later step.
senses.whyCN: 正式写作用它标示较晚的一步。

intro.en: Subsequently is the adverb built from subsequent.
intro.cn: subsequently 是由 subsequent 构成的副词。

items.en: Sub meant after.
items.cn: sub 意为在后。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow.

items.en: Subsequent described what came later.
items.cn: subsequent 形容随后而来的。

items.en: -Ly turned it into an adverb.
items.cn: 后缀 -ly 使它成为副词。

items.en: Subsequently became common in reports.
items.cn: subsequently 在报告中变得常见。

note.en: Subsequently is compared with look-alike words and with other time words.
note.cn: 把 subsequently 与形近词以及其他时间词作比较。

entries.definition: as a result
entries.definitionCN: 因此

entries.definition: a sequence within a sequence
entries.definitionCN: 子序列

entries.definition: powerful speaking

entries.definition: at a later time
entries.definitionCN: 后来

entries.definition: after an event

normalIntro.en: Subsequently marks the next scene after the one just shown.
normalIntro.cn: subsequently 标出刚演完这一幕之后的下一幕。

normal.en: He subsequently moved to another city.
normal.cn: 他随后搬到了另一座城市。

normal.en: She subsequently became a teacher.

abstract.en: Subsequently is a small word that keeps time moving.
abstract.cn: subsequently 是个小词，却让时间继续往前走。

abstract.en: What happens subsequently is often the real story.
abstract.cn: 随后发生的事，往往才是真正的故事。

abstract.en: The report names the cause; subsequently names the echo.

dict_mnemonic.text: subsequently 是「随后、后来」，由 subsequent 加 -ly 构成；常用于叙述顺序，如 subsequently became、subsequently found、subsequently confirmed。

root: 由形容词 subsequent（随后的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成；其词根源自拉丁语 sequi（跟随），因此表示在前一件事之后发生。

sensesIntro.en: Subsequently means after that, or later on.

core.en: A marker placed on the next step in time.

branches.en: The study was subsequently published.

branches.en: The next event and the later report share the word.

definition_en: a flat round Italian bread base covered with tomato, cheese and other toppings and baked in an oven
core_image: 圆饼上铺满番茄、奶酪和浇头，从砖炉里端出来还冒着热气
scene: 深夜的厨房里，他从纸盒里抽出最后一块还温热的饼。 He reheated the leftover pizza for a midnight snack.
sceneCN: 这里是「比萨饼」（第 1 个义项：一种意式烤饼）；句意为他把剩下的比萨加热当宵夜。画面就是那块铺满浇头的圆饼。

derivatives.zh: pizza 加意大利语后缀 -eria 构成，义为「比萨店」
意大利语借词，义为「做比萨的师傅」

senses.title: The Italian baked dish
senses.definition: a flat round bread baked with tomato, cheese and toppings
senses.definitionCN: 铺了番茄、奶酪和浇头烤成的圆形薄饼
senses.example: We shared a large pizza with mushrooms and ham.
senses.exampleCN: 我们分吃了一个大个的蘑菇火腿比萨。
senses.why: The word named the southern Italian street food and travelled with emigrants around the world.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原本指南意大利的街头吃食，随移民走遍世界。

senses.title: A serving or whole pie
senses.definition: one whole pizza, ordered or baked as a unit
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个单位订购或烤制的一整个比萨
senses.example: Two pizzas should be enough for six people.
senses.exampleCN: 两个比萨够六个人吃了。
senses.why: The dish name doubles as a counting unit, like cake or pie in English eating speech.
senses.whyCN: 菜名兼任计数单位，就像英语饮食口语里的 cake 或 pie。

senses.title: Pizza as a shared occasion
senses.definition: the informal meal or event built around eating pizza together
senses.definitionCN: 围绕一起吃比萨展开的随意聚餐
senses.example: Movie night means pizza and bad films.
senses.exampleCN: 电影之夜就意味着比萨和烂片。
senses.why: Because the food is cheap, shareable and casual, its name came to stand for the easy gathering itself.
senses.whyCN: 这种食物便宜、可分食、随意，它的名字便代表了那种轻松的聚会本身。

intro.en: Pizza is an Italian dialect word of uncertain deeper origin, first recorded in Naples and carried worldwide by emigration.
intro.cn: pizza 是个意大利方言词，更深的来源不确定，最早见于那不勒斯，随移民传遍世界。

items.en: The word appears in Neapolitan dialect in the tenth-century Latinised form picea, maybe linked to pitta bread.
items.cn: 该词见于那不勒斯方言，十世纪拉丁化形式为 picea，可能与皮塔饼有关。

items.en: Some link it to Latin pinsere, to pound dough; others to a Lombardic word for bite; no theory is certain.
items.cn: 有人把它联系到拉丁语 pinsere（捣面团），也有人联系伦巴第语的「咬」；诸说均无定论。

items.en: In nineteenth-century Naples the modern tomato pizza took shape as street food.
items.cn: 十九世纪的那不勒斯，现代番茄比萨作为街头食品成形。

items.en: Italian emigrants carried pizzerias to America, where the dish conquered global taste.
items.cn: 意大利移民把比萨店带到美洲，这道菜征服了全球味蕾。

items.en: English borrowed the word unchanged, pluralising it with a plain -s.
items.cn: 英语原样借用该词，只加了普通的 -s 构成复数。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers look-alikes and the Italian food family; the near-meaning group gathers shareable flat foods.
note.cn: 形近组收形近词与意大利食物家族；近义组收可分享的扁平食物。

entries.definition: The shop where pizza is made and sold.
entries.definitionCN: 制作并出售比萨的店。

entries.definition: A round Middle Eastern flatbread; close in sound and possibly in distant history, but a different food.
entries.definitionCN: 中东圆形面饼；读音相近、来历或有远亲，但是另一种食物。

entries.definition: An open town square in Italy; one letter apart from pizza and unrelated in meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 意大利的城镇广场；与 pizza 仅差一个字母，意义无关。

entries.definition: Any thin flat bread baked without rising agents.
entries.definitionCN: 各种不加发酵剂烤成的扁平面包。

entries.definition: An Italian folded turnover, pizza's closed cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 意式对折烤饼，比萨的「合上盖」亲戚。

entries.definition: A French savoury tart with egg filling, served in the same casual way.
entries.definitionCN: 法式咸蛋挞，同样以随意的场合上桌。

normalIntro.en: One image and one borrowed word: memory leans on the picture and the Italian shop suffix.
normalIntro.cn: 一个意象、一个借词：记忆靠画面和意大利语的店名后缀。

normal.en: Pizza, pizzeria, pizzaiolo: the food, the shop, the man who makes it.
normal.cn: pizza、pizzeria、pizzaiolo：食物、店、做饼的师傅。

normal.en: Piazza is the square, pizza is the pie — one letter separates the two Italian icons.
normal.cn: piazza 是广场，pizza 是大饼——一个字母隔开两件意大利象征。

normal.en: The plural is plain English: two pizzas, no fuss.
normal.cn: 复数是普通英语：two pizzas，毫不费劲。

normal.en: Deep-pan or thin-crust, the word covers every thickness.
normal.cn: 厚底或薄脆，这个词一视同仁。

normal.en: Pizza night means the gathering, not just the dish.
normal.cn: pizza night 指的是那场聚会，不止是那块饼。

abstract.en: A steaming circle pulled from a brick oven, cheese stretching as a slice lifts.
abstract.cn: 砖炉里端出的热气腾腾的圆饼，掀起一角时奶酪拉出丝。

abstract.en: A square cardboard box, opened at midnight on a sofa.
abstract.cn: 深夜沙发上打开的方形纸盒。

abstract.en: Hands reaching into the middle of the table, all at once.
abstract.cn: 几只手同时伸向桌子中央。

examples.en: A hot pizza arrived twenty minutes after we ordered.
examples.cn: 我们下单二十分钟后，热比萨送到了。

examples.en: The pizzeria on the corner sells pizza by the slice.

senses.title: Farming as a whole
senses.definition: the practice of growing crops and raising animals for food, fibre or other products
senses.definitionCN: 种植作物、饲养牲畜以获取食物、纤维或其他产品的生产活动
senses.example: Agriculture shaped the landscape of this plain for thousands of years.
senses.exampleCN: 农业塑造了这片平原的地貌，已持续数千年。
senses.why: Latin ager 'field' plus cultura 'cultivation' says the whole thing at once: the field and the work done on it, taken as one enterprise.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ager「田地」加 cultura「耕作」，一句话就说全了：那块田加上对它做的事，合起来当作一项生产事业，就是「农业」。

senses.title: The science and technique of farming
senses.definition: the systematic knowledge and technique of cultivating soil, crops and livestock
senses.definitionCN: 关于耕作土壤、栽培作物与饲养牲畜的系统知识与技术
senses.example: She studied agriculture for four years before returning to the family farm.
senses.exampleCN: 她学了四年农学，然后回到家里的农场。
senses.why: Cultura already meant both tilling and training; once the tilling is set out as teachable knowledge, the word becomes a discipline.
senses.whyCN: cultura 本来就兼指「耕作」与「培养、训练」；当耕作被整理成可以教、可以学的知识时，这个词就成了一门学科。

senses.title: Tilling the soil
senses.definition: the physical work of preparing and cultivating land, the oldest and most literal sense
senses.definitionCN: 翻整与照料土地的具体劳作，是最古老、最字面的义项
senses.example: In the old handbook, agriculture meant ploughing, sowing and harvest in turn.
senses.exampleCN: 在那本旧手册里，「agriculture」依次指耕地、播种与收获。
senses.why: This is the etymological core laid bare: ager is the plot, cultura is the turning and tending, and together they name work done with hands.
senses.whyCN: 这是词源最直白的一面：ager 是那块地，cultura 是翻土与照料，合起来就是「用手在一块地上干活」。

senses.title: The farming sector
senses.definition: farming as a branch of the economy or a field of government policy
senses.definitionCN: 作为国民经济的一个门类或政府政策领域来看的农业
senses.example: Subsidies to agriculture account for a large share of the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 对农业的补贴占了预算的很大一部分。
senses.why: When tilling is counted, taxed and subsidised, the field becomes a line in a table, and the word shifts from the work to the sector.
senses.whyCN: 当耕作要被统计、征税和补贴时，田地就变成了表格里的一栏，这个词也就从田间劳作转指整个产业部门。

senses.title: Farming as a livelihood
senses.definition: farming considered as the means by which a place or a people lives
senses.definitionCN: 作为某地或某群人赖以为生的手段来看的农业
senses.example: For most families here, agriculture is the only source of income.
senses.exampleCN: 对这里的大多数家庭来说，农业是唯一的收入来源。
senses.why: The field feeds the people who work it, so the same word can name not a technique or a sector but the living that land provides.
senses.whyCN: 田地不只长出粮食，也养活靠它的人；因此这个词还可以不指技术、不指部门，而指土地提供的那份生计。

intro.en: Agriculture is a Latin compound of ager 'field' and cultura 'cultivation', and it entered English as a bookish word for the tilling of land.
intro.cn: agriculture 是拉丁语 ager「田地」与 cultura「耕作」的复合词，进入英语时是一个书面色彩较浓的「耕地」之词。

items.en: *h₂éǵros is the reconstructed root for 'field'; it is the common ancestor of Latin ager, Greek agros and English acre, and the reconstruction is marked as such.
items.cn: 重构形式 *h₂éǵros 表示「田地」，是拉丁语 ager、希腊语 agros 与英语 acre 的共同祖先；此处标明它是重构形式。

items.en: Ager meant 'field, land, countryside'; its genitive agri shows the stem agr- that appears in compounds.
items.cn: ager 意为「田地、土地、乡野」；其属格 agri 显示出复合词中出现的词干 agr-。

items.en: Colere meant 'to till, cultivate, inhabit, worship'; the noun cultura named cultivation and, by extension, care and training.
items.cn: colere 意为「耕作、栽培、居住、敬奉」；名词 cultura 表示耕作，并引申出照料与培养。

items.en: Ager plus cultura formed agricultura, 'the cultivation of land', a word already used by Roman writers on farming.
items.cn: ager 加 cultura 构成 agricultura「土地耕作」，罗马的农书作者已经使用这个词。

items.en: English agriculture is recorded from the fifteenth century, probably through French; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语 agriculture 自十五世纪起有记录，可能经法语传入；确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: The word widened from work in the field to a science, an industry, a ministry and a subject at university.
items.cn: 这个词从田间的劳作扩展为一门科学、一个产业、一个政府部门，以及大学里的一门专业。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the ager- root, either through Latin or through Greek and Old English; the near-meaning group gathers narrower words for working the land.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在 ager- 词根上的词，或经拉丁语，或经希腊语与古英语；近义组收范围更窄的「种地」类词。

entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「农业的、农艺的」，由本词加后缀 -al 构成。

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农学家、务农者」，由本词加后缀 -ist 构成。

entries.definition: The science of crop production; Greek agros 'field' matches Latin ager, so the root is shared but the path differs.

entries.definition: A unit of land area; Old English æcer came from the same Indo-European word for a field.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「英亩」；古英语 æcer 与 ager 同出印欧语表示「田地」的词。

entries.definition: Farming treated as a large commercial industry; a modern compound with agriculture as its first half.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农业综合企业」，指把农业当作大型商业产业来经营，是 agriculture 与 business 构成的现代复合词。

entries.definition: The everyday word for growing crops and keeping animals, including the business side.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「务农、耕作」，是最日常的说法，也包含经营的一面。

entries.definition: The careful management of soil, crops or animals; old-fashioned and formal.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「农牧管理、耕作」，强调精心经营，语气正式且偏旧。

entries.definition: The act of preparing land and growing crops; narrower than agriculture.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「耕作、栽培」，只指整地与种植这一动作，范围比 agriculture 窄。

entries.definition: The growing of garden plants, fruit and vegetables, on a smaller scale than agriculture.

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin halves ager and cultura, the recorded family, and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁语两半 ager 与 cultura、有记录的词族，以及这个词实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Ager is 'field' and cultura is 'cultivation': agriculture is literally field-cultivation.
normal.cn: ager 是「田地」，cultura 是「耕作」：agriculture 字面就是「耕田」。

normal.en: The same field root appears in acre and, through Greek, in agronomy.
normal.cn: 同一个「田地」词根还出现在 acre 里，并经由希腊语出现在 agronomy 里。

normal.en: Cultura also gives culture: both words are about tending something and bringing it on.
normal.cn: cultura 还给出 culture：两个词都与「照料并让它成长」有关。

normal.en: Agricultural and agriculturist are the two common family forms.
normal.cn: agricultural 与 agriculturist 是这一词族最常用的两个形式。

normal.en: The Ministry of Agriculture is the sector sense: farming counted as a branch of government.
normal.cn: the Ministry of Agriculture 用的是部门义：农业被算作政府的一个分支。

abstract.en: The word joins two halves: the land that is given, and the care that is added to it.

core_image: 印在作品门口的名字；一枚挂在名下的法律标签
scene: 封面上烫金的书名在灯下闪光。 She read the title of the novel aloud.
sceneCN: 这里 title 是「标题」（第 1 个义项：作品的名称）；句意：她大声读出那本小说的书名。

derivatives.zh: en- + title，义为「使有权；给……题名」
entitle 加 -ment，义为「应得的权利；津贴」

senses.title: The name of a work
senses.definition: the name given to a book, film, painting or piece of music
senses.definitionCN: 书籍、电影、画作或乐曲的名称
senses.example: The title of the film is three words long.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影的片名有三个词。
senses.why: The core image is a name posted at the door of a work.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是挂在作品门口的名字。

senses.title: A name of rank or office
senses.definition: a word such as Doctor or Professor used before a name to show rank
senses.definitionCN: 置于姓名前表示身份的称呼，如 Doctor、Professor
senses.example: How should I address you — what title do you use?
senses.exampleCN: 我该怎么称呼您——您用什么头衔？
senses.why: The name on the door becomes the label on the person.
senses.whyCN: 门上的名字变成人身上的标签。

senses.title: Legal ownership
senses.definition: the legal right to own property, especially land or a car
senses.definitionCN: 拥有财产（尤指土地、车辆）的法定权利
senses.example: The title to the farm is held in trust.
senses.exampleCN: 农场产权由信托持有。
senses.why: Ownership is written as a label fixed to the thing owned.
senses.whyCN: 所有权被写成固定在物上的标签。

senses.title: A championship
senses.definition: the position of winning a competition, defended in later contests
senses.definitionCN: 竞赛夺魁的地位，可在后续赛事中卫冕
senses.example: She defends her title next month.
senses.exampleCN: 她下个月卫冕冠军。
senses.why: Championship is a label of rank held and guarded.
senses.whyCN: 冠军是一枚被持有和守护的等级标签。

senses.title: To give a name to a work
senses.definition: to give a title to a book, film or section
senses.definitionCN: 为书籍、影片或章节定名
senses.example: The chapter is titled Broken Glass.
senses.exampleCN: 该章题为「碎玻璃」。
senses.why: The posted name becomes an act of posting.
senses.whyCN: 门上的名字变成「挂名」这个动作。

senses.title: A written work as a catalogue item
senses.definition: a book or publication counted as one item in a list or library
senses.definitionCN: 在清单或图书馆中被计为一条的书籍或出版物
senses.example: The press issues twenty new titles a year.
senses.exampleCN: 该出版社每年推出二十个新书品种。
senses.why: A work is counted by its name-tag on the shelf.
senses.whyCN: 一部作品按书架上的名字标签被清点。

senses.title: A claim based on right
senses.definition: a ground or basis of right, as in the old phrase by the title of law
senses.definitionCN: 权利的依据，如旧语 by the title of law
senses.example: Their claim has no title in law.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的主张在法律上没有依据。
senses.why: The legal label extends to any ground of right.
senses.whyCN: 法律标签扩展为一切权利的依据。

senses.title: Titles in cards and church offices
senses.definition: in law and church use, the office or church from which a cleric takes his designation
senses.definitionCN: 法律与教会用语中，圣职人员所系的职位或教堂名义
senses.example: The priest held his title from an old abbey.
senses.exampleCN: 这位神父的职衔系于一座古老修道院。
senses.why: Rank labels branch into institutional forms.
senses.whyCN: 等级标签延伸出制度化的形态。

intro.en: Title comes from Old French title and Latin titulus, an inscription or label placed over something, which grew into names of works, ranks and ownership.
intro.cn: title 经古法语来自拉丁语 titulus「铭文、标签」，置于某物之上的标记，发展出作品名、头衔与产权诸义。

items.en: Titulus meant an inscription, a plaque or label fixed above a thing.
items.cn: 拉丁语 titulus 指铭文，固定于物上的牌子或标签。

items.en: Title kept the senses of inscription and chapter heading.
items.cn: 古法语 title 保留铭文与章节标题之义。

items.en: Title named book headings and legal grounds of right.
items.cn: 中古英语 title 兼指书名与法律权利依据。

items.en: Title spread to ranks and forms of address.
items.cn: 十五世纪 title 扩展至头衔与称谓。

items.en: The verb to title appeared with printed books.
items.cn: 随着印刷书籍出现，动词 title 产生。

items.en: Modern usage spans works, rank, property and championships.
items.cn: 现代用法涵盖作品、头衔、产权与冠军。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike -itle words; the second sorts name-and-right neighbours.
note.cn: 第一组是 -itle 形近词；第二组列出名称与权利义的近邻。

entries.definition: small in size; spelled close but a different word
entries.definitionCN: 小的；拼写相近而非同词

entries.definition: a tiny mark or dot in writing
entries.definitionCN: 书写中的小点；微小的记号

entries.definition: a secondary title or printed translation of dialogue
entries.definitionCN: 副标题；字幕

entries.definition: words written at the top of a page or section
entries.definitionCN: 标题；页首字样

entries.definition: a signed legal document proving ownership
entries.definitionCN: 契约；产权证书

entries.definition: a position in a scale of status or authority
entries.definitionCN: 级别；地位

normalIntro.en: Real links: the title of a book, a job title, title deed, and winning the title.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：书名、职位名称、地契，以及夺冠。

normal.en: A title is the label fixed above the door of a work.
normal.cn: title 是挂在作品门楣上的标签。

normal.en: A job title pins the same label to a person.
normal.cn: 职位名称把同样的标签钉在人身上。

normal.en: A title deed is ownership written as a label.
normal.cn: 地契就是写成标签的所有权。

normal.en: Winning the title is holding the champion's label.
normal.cn: 夺冠就是握住冠军的标签。

normal.en: Entitle hands someone the right the label carries.
normal.cn: entitle 把标签所载的权利交到某人手中。

abstract.en: Every title is a short inscription that opens a claim.
abstract.cn: 每个 title 都是开启一项主张的简短铭文。

abstract.en: Names name things; titles give them standing.
abstract.cn: 名字称呼事物，title 给它们名分。

abstract.en: To hold a title is to keep the plaque polished.
abstract.cn: 持有头衔，就是把那块牌子时时擦亮。

examples.en: The title page lists the publisher and the year.
examples.cn: 扉页列出出版社与年份。

examples.en: He held the boxing title for three years.
examples.cn: 他保持了三年拳击冠军头衔。

examples.en: The house is titled in her name.
examples.cn: 这栋房子的产权登记在她名下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「抬头」——抬头上写的正是标题与头衔 → title 标题；头衔

root: 单一词干：拉丁语 titulus「铭文、标签」，经古法语 title 进入英语。核心是「置于其上的标记」，由物名而人名，由名分而产权。

sensesIntro.en: Title begins as an inscription and grows into names, ranks, ownership and championships.
sensesIntro.cn: title 始于一块铭牌，长成书名、头衔、产权与冠军。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a label fixed above a thing, marking name, rank or right.
core.cn: 核心意象：置于其上的标签，标记者名称、等级或权利。

branches.en: Names of works, given and counted.
branches.cn: 作品之名，被赋予与被清点。

branches.en: Rank labels and institutional offices.
branches.cn: 等级标签与制度职衔。

branches.en: Ownership and grounds of right.
branches.cn: 产权与权利依据。

branches.en: The champion's guarded label.
branches.cn: 被守护的冠军标签。

branches.en: The act of naming.
branches.cn: 命名的动作。

intro.en: Title is a Latin stem; its items show prefixes and compounds built on the label idea.
intro.cn: title 是拉丁词干；条目展示围绕「标签」观念的前缀与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin titulus underlies the whole family; the prefix lines below share it.
latinIntro.cn: 整个词族都建立在拉丁语 titulus 之上；下列前缀词均与之相关。

items.meaning: to give a right or a name to
items.example: The ticket entitles you to a free seat.
items.exampleCN: 这张票让你有权免费入座。

items.meaning: an official right to a benefit
items.exampleCN: 带薪休假是应得的权利。

items.meaning: a secondary title or film dialogue translation
items.example: We watched the film with subtitles.
items.exampleCN: 我们开着字幕看了那部电影。

items.meaning: the document proving ownership of land
items.example: The title deed is in the safe.

items.meaning: the page showing a book's full name
items.example: The title page carries the printer's mark.

items.meaning: holding a title without the full duties
items.example: He is the titular head of the firm.

items.meaning: the official name of a position
items.example: Her job title is Senior Analyst.
items.exampleCN: 她的职位是资深分析师。

items.meaning: the current champion or owner of a title
items.meaningCN: 冠军保持者；头衔持有人

definition_en: a line that bends smoothly, or to bend and move along such a line
core_image: 一条山路贴着山腰画出一道长长的弧
scene: 山路在前面拐了一个大弯，消失在树后。 The road curves sharply to the left.
sceneCN: 这里 curves 是 curve 的第三人称单数，指「转弯」（第 2 个义项：道路弯折）；句意是这条路向左急转。

senses.title: A smooth bend
senses.definition: a line that bends without any sharp angles
senses.definitionCN: 没有任何尖锐折角的弯线
senses.example: The graph shows a smooth curve.
senses.exampleCN: 图表上是一条平滑的曲线。
senses.why: A line that keeps changing direction gently is still one unbroken line.
senses.whyCN: 一条不断轻轻改变方向的线，仍然是不断的一整条。

senses.title: A bend in a road
senses.definition: a place where a road, river, or path turns
senses.definitionCN: 道路、河流或小径转弯的地方
senses.example: Slow down before the curve.
senses.exampleCN: 过弯道前要减速。
senses.why: What is straight on a map can bend on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 地图上笔直的路，到了地上也可能弯。

senses.title: To bend
senses.definition: to move or make something move in a curved line
senses.definitionCN: 沿曲线移动，或使某物沿曲线移动
senses.example: The path curves around the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 小径绕着湖弯过去。
senses.why: Anything that avoids an obstacle must go round it.
senses.whyCN: 凡是绕开障碍的东西，都得弯过去。

intro.en: Curve comes from Latin curvus, bent or crooked, which passed through the English of the seventeenth century.
intro.cn: curve 源自拉丁语 curvus（弯的、曲的），在十七世纪进入英语。

items.en: Curvus described anything bent out of a straight line.
items.cn: curvus 形容一切偏离直线的弯。

items.en: Curvare meant to bend something into a bow.
items.cn: curvare 意为把东西弯成弓形。

items.en: Curve first named a bent line in geometry.
items.cn: curve 最初指几何中的弯线。

items.en: It spread to roads, rivers, and the human body.
items.cn: 它扩展到道路、河流和人的身体。

items.en: Curve also became a verb meaning to move in a bend.
items.cn: curve 也变成动词，表示沿弯线移动。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the cur- opening, and the meaning group names other kinds of bending.
note.cn: 形近组共享 cur- 开头，近义组列出其他表示弯折的说法。

entries.definition: words that wish harm on someone
entries.definitionCN: 希望别人遭殃的话

entries.definition: to cut shapes into wood or stone
entries.definitionCN: 在木头或石头上刻出形状

entries.definition: to keep something under control
entries.definitionCN: 把某事控制在范围内

entries.definition: to make a straight thing crooked
entries.definitionCN: 把直的东西弄弯

entries.definition: a curved line like part of a circle
entries.definitionCN: 像圆的一部分那样的弯线

entries.definition: a change of direction
entries.definitionCN: 方向的改变

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a line that leaves the ruler and end with a road that hides itself behind trees.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一条离开直尺的线开始，落到一条藏在树后的路。

normal.en: A curve is a straight line that changed its mind slowly.
normal.cn: 曲线，就是慢慢改变主意的直线。

normal.en: Roads bend because hills will not move.
normal.cn: 路会弯，是因为山不肯让开。

normal.en: A learning curve bends upward because skill grows unevenly.
normal.cn: 学习曲线往上弯，因为本事长得不均匀。

normal.en: To be ahead of the curve is to turn before the road does.
normal.cn: 领先于潮流，就是在路转弯之前先转。

normal.en: If it never holds a straight line, it is a curve.
normal.cn: 如果它从不肯走直线，它就是曲线。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil line leaning away from a ruler.
abstract.cn: 想象一条铅笔线慢慢偏离直尺。

abstract.en: Picture headlights sweeping across a hillside turn.
abstract.cn: 想象车灯扫过山腰的弯道。

abstract.en: Picture a river bending around a field of reeds.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河绕过芦苇地弯过去。

examples.en: The graph shows a smooth curve.
examples.cn: 图表上是一条平滑的曲线。

examples.en: Slow down before the curve.
examples.cn: 过弯道前要减速。

examples.en: The path curves around the lake.
examples.cn: 小径绕着湖弯过去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 curve 记成「弯」：路不肯直着走，就画出一道弧，这道弧就是曲线。

root: 源自拉丁语 curvus（弯的），动词为 curvare（使弯成弓形）；本义是偏离直线的弯，先用于几何，后用于道路、河流与身体。

sensesIntro.en: From a bent line on paper, to a bend in the road, to the act of bending around something.
sensesIntro.cn: 从纸上的一条弯线，到路上的一个弯，再到绕过障碍的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line that leaves the straight and bends gently away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条离开直线、轻轻弯出去的线。

branches.en: The pure shape is a line with no sharp corner.
branches.cn: 最纯粹的形状，是一条没有尖角的线。

branches.en: On the ground the same shape becomes a turn in the road.
branches.cn: 到了地面上，同一个形状变成路上的弯。

branches.en: To curve is to trace that line with your own movement.
branches.cn: 弯曲，就是用自己的运动把那条线走出来。

branches.en: Drawn or driven, the bend keeps the same geometry.
branches.cn: 画出来的弯和开出来的弯，几何形状是一样的。

branches.en: A road curves because travellers must curve with it.
branches.cn: 路会弯，是因为走的人也得跟着弯。

intro.en: Curve belongs to the Latin curvus family, where bending grows into geometry, roads, and the body.
intro.cn: curve 属于拉丁语 curvus 这一族，「弯」在这里长成几何、道路和身体。

latinIntro.en: The Latin curvus, bent, and curvare, to bend, stand under this family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 curvus（弯的）与 curvare（使弯）是这一族词的根。

items.example: The road makes a wide curve.
The blade has a curved edge.

items.exampleCN: 一条弯曲的小路通向坡上。

items.example: The curvature of the earth is slight.
The road turned curvy near the coast.
items.exampleCN: 路在海岸附近变得弯弯曲曲。

items.meaning: a ball that bends, or a surprise
items.example: Life threw him a curve ball.
items.exampleCN: 生活给他出了个意外难题。

items.meaning: the rate at which skill grows
items.example: The job has a steep learning curve.
items.exampleCN: 这份工作的学习曲线很陡。

items.example: The train took the undercurve slowly.
items.exampleCN: 火车慢慢驶过下方的弯道。

definition_zh: 冰柜；冰箱冷冻室；冷藏库
definition_en: a machine or room used for keeping food frozen at a very low temperature
core_image: 一台低沉嗡嗡作响的柜子，门一开便涌出白雾，里面的食物冻得梆硬
scene: 清晨的厨房里，妈妈打开柜门取出一袋冻豆子，白雾扑面而来。 She took the last bag of peas out of the freezer.
sceneCN: 这里 freezer 是「冰柜；冷冻室」（第 1 个义项：低温冷冻食物的设备）；句意是她从冰柜里取出最后一袋豌豆。

collocations.phrase: take something out of the freezer
a chest freezer with a broken seal

derivatives.zh: 基础动词，义为「结冰；冷冻；冻结」，freezer 由其加名词后缀 -er 构成
freeze 的过去分词转形容词，义为「冰冻的；冷冻的」
freeze 加 -ing 构成，义为「极冷的；冰点以下的」

senses.title: A device that keeps food frozen
senses.definition: a household appliance or a compartment that stores food below freezing point
senses.definitionCN: 把食物储存在冰点以下的家用电器或冰箱的一个隔层
senses.example: The freezer hums quietly in the corner of the kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 冰柜在厨房角落里低声嗡嗡运转。
senses.why: The verb freeze names the action, and -er names the agent or tool that performs it.
senses.whyCN: 动词 freeze 表示「冷冻」这一动作，后缀 -er 表示执行该动作的工具。

senses.title: An industrial cold-storage room
senses.definition: a large room or storehouse where goods are kept at freezing temperatures
senses.definitionCN: 把货物保存在冷冻温度下的大房间或仓库
senses.example: Workers wear thick coats inside the meat freezer.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在肉类冷藏库里要穿上厚外套。
senses.why: The same tool-word scales up from a home appliance to an industrial chamber.
senses.whyCN: 同一个工具名词由家用电器放大为工业级冷冻库房。

senses.title: A stockpile of frozen food
senses.titleCN: 冻品储备；冰柜里的存粮
senses.definition: the supply of frozen food kept in such a device, spoken of as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 存放在冷冻设备里的冻品总量，被当作一个整体来谈论
senses.example: A well-stocked freezer saved us from cooking every night.
senses.exampleCN: 存满冻品的冰柜让我们不必每晚做饭。
senses.why: From naming the container, usage shifts to what the container holds.
senses.whyCN: 由指称容器转指容器所装之物，即冰柜里的冻品储备。

intro.en: Freezer is a modern agent noun: the old verb freeze plus the tool suffix -er.
intro.cn: freezer 是一个现代的工具名词：古老动词 freeze 加上工具后缀 -er。

items.en: The verb goes back to Proto-Germanic *frezaną, generally reconstructed as meaning to freeze, related to frost.
items.cn: 该动词可追溯至原始日耳曼语 *frezaną，一般认为重构义为「结冰」，与 frost（霜）同源。

items.en: Old English frēosan meant to freeze, used of water, weather, and people who felt cold.
items.cn: 古英语 frēosan 意为「结冰；冻僵」，既可用于水与天气，也可用于感到寒冷的人。

items.en: Middle English fresen kept the same core meaning and produced the past participle frozen.
items.cn: 中古英语 fresen 保持同一核心词义，并产生了过去分词 frozen。

items.en: With ice cutting and early refrigeration, agent nouns like freezer appeared for machines and cold rooms.
items.cn: 随着采冰业与早期制冷技术的出现，freezer 这类工具名词开始指机器与低温库房。

items.en: Electric household refrigeration made freezer a normal kitchen word, at first for the freezer compartment of a fridge.
items.cn: 家用电制冷的普及让 freezer 成为寻常厨房用词，最初指冰箱的冷冻室。

items.en: Today freezer covers both the standalone chest freezer and the freezer compartment inside a refrigerator.
items.cn: 如今 freezer 既指独立的卧式冰柜，也指冰箱内置的冷冻室。

note.en: Freezer belongs to the cold chain of words; keep it apart from fridge, which cools rather than freezes.
note.cn: freezer 属于一组「冷」词；注意与 fridge 区分——fridge 是冷藏而非冷冻。

entries.definition: very cold, at or below freezing point
entries.definitionCN: 极冷的；冰点以下的，与 freezer 同根

entries.definition: comparative of fresh; only spelled somewhat near freezer, root is unrelated
entries.definitionCN: fresh 的比较级；只是拼写与 freezer 略近，词根无关

entries.definition: to freeze again, especially thawed food
entries.definitionCN: 重新冷冻，尤指解冻后的食物，与 freezer 同根

entries.definition: a refrigerator that keeps food cool but not frozen
entries.definitionCN: 冰箱，只冷藏不冷冻，与 freezer 相邻但分工不同

entries.definition: the formal word for a cooling appliance
entries.definitionCN: 冰箱的正式说法，与 freezer 相对的是冷藏功能

entries.definition: an older cabinet cooled with ice blocks
entries.definitionCN: 旧式用冰块降温的柜子，是 freezer 的前身概念

normalIntro.en: Read the word as freeze plus er and the meaning falls out.
normalIntro.cn: 把这个词读成 freeze 加 er，词义便一目了然。

normal.en: freeze + -er: the machine that does the freezing.
normal.cn: freeze + -er：执行「冷冻」动作的机器。

normal.en: Same pattern as cleaner, cooker, printer: tool nouns from verbs.
normal.cn: 构词与 cleaner、cooker、printer 相同：动词加后缀成工具名词。

normal.en: Pair it with fridge: fridge cools, freezer freezes.

definition_zh: 承认；入场费；进入许可；录取；入院；供认
definition_en: the act of accepting that something is true, or the right, permission or money needed to enter a place or an institution
core_image: 门口的一道闸：一边放人进来，一边把不愿说的事放进来
scene: 剧院门口排起长队，售票窗上贴着手写的价目。 Admission is twenty dollars for adults and half price for children.
sceneCN: 这里 admission 指进场要付的钱（第 2 个义项：入场费）；句意为成人入场二十美元，儿童半价。

pos.zh: 名词：承认；入场费；进入许可；录取；入院

derivatives.zh: 同一词族的动词，义为「承认；准许进入」，admission 正由它的拉丁名词形式而来
由动词加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「进入权；进入」，多用于正式告示
由本词加形容词后缀 -ible 构成，义为「可采纳的；可接受的」
由否定前缀 in- 加 admissible 构成，义为「不可采纳的；不予接受的」

senses.title: The act of accepting that something is true
senses.definition: the act of agreeing that something is true, especially something you would rather not accept
senses.definitionCN: 同意某事为真，尤指自己本不愿接受的事
senses.example: His admission that he had copied the essay shocked the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他承认那篇文章是抄来的，这让全班都吃了一惊。
senses.why: Admission is the noun of admittere, 'to let in': a fact you had been keeping outside the door is finally allowed through, and the word names that letting-in.
senses.whyCN: admission 是 admittere「放进来」的名词形式：一个被你挡在门外很久的事实终于被放进来，这个词命名的正是这次「放行」。

senses.title: The money paid to enter a place
senses.definition: the amount of money that you must pay to enter a museum, theatre, sports ground or similar place
senses.definitionCN: 进入博物馆、剧院、体育场等场所必须支付的费用
senses.example: Admission to the exhibition costs ten pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这个展览的入场费是十英镑。
senses.why: Once the letting-in becomes a service, it acquires a price: the door that could open for nothing can also sell the right of passage, and the price takes the name of the act itself.
senses.whyCN: 当「放人进来」变成一项服务，它就有了价钱：这扇门本来可以无偿打开，也可以把通行权卖出去，而这个价钱直接沿用了「放行」这个动作的名字。

senses.title: Permission or the right to enter
senses.definition: permission or the right to enter a place, join a group, or be present at an event
senses.definitionCN: 进入某场所、加入某团体或出席某活动的许可与权利
senses.example: No admission without a ticket.
senses.exampleCN: 没有票不得入场。
senses.why: This is the literal core of the Latin word: ad- means to and mittere means send, so admission is the state of being sent in through a doorway.
senses.whyCN: 这是拉丁词的字面核心：ad- 表示「向」，mittere 表示「送」，admission 就是「被送进门内」的那种状态。

senses.title: Acceptance into a school or college
senses.definition: the act of accepting someone as a student or member of an institution, or the process of doing so
senses.definitionCN: 接纳某人为学生或机构成员的行为，或这项工作本身的流程
senses.example: The college changed its admission rules for overseas applicants.
senses.exampleCN: 学院修改了海外申请者的录取规则。
senses.why: A school is a door too: the noun for entering a building came to describe passing the academic gate, and in the plural it names the office that decides who gets through.
senses.whyCN: 学校也是一扇门：原本描述「进楼」的名词被用来描述通过学业这道门，而复数形式还指决定放谁进来的那个招生部门。

senses.title: Being taken into hospital
senses.definition: the act of taking a patient into hospital so that they can be cared for
senses.definitionCN: 把病人收进医院接受照护的行为
senses.example: Her admission to hospital followed a week of chest pain.
senses.exampleCN: 胸口疼了一个星期之后，她住进了医院。
senses.why: Medical language fixes the same image to one building: the hospital is the door, and the patient sent through it becomes an admission on the ward list.
senses.whyCN: 医学语境把同一个意象固定到一座建筑上：医院就是那扇门，被送进去的病人就成了病房名单上的一条「入院」记录。

senses.title: A statement used as evidence in court
senses.definition: a formal statement in which someone accepts that they did something wrong, which may be used as evidence against them
senses.definitionCN: 正式承认自己做过错事的陈述，可能被用作对自己不利的证据
senses.example: The detective read the suspect's admission aloud to the jury.
senses.exampleCN: 警探把嫌疑人的供认当庭念给了陪审团听。
senses.why: In court the thing let in is a statement: once the record opens to it, the admission belongs to the case, so the legal use leans on the same doorway image.
senses.whyCN: 在法庭上被放行的是陈述本身：记录一旦对它敞开，这份承认就成了案件的一部分，法律用法仍靠那扇门的意象支撑。

intro.en: Admission is the Latin noun of admittere, 'to send in', and it entered English through French with the doorway image intact.
intro.cn: admission 是 admittere「送进去」的拉丁名词，经法语进入英语时，「门」的意象依然完整。

items.en: Mittere meant 'to send, let go', and it is also the source of mission, permit and transmit.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送出、放开」，也是 mission、permit 与 transmit 的来源。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus mittere formed admittere, 'to send to, let in, allow to enter'.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 mittere 构成 admittere，意为「送到、放进来、准许进入」。

items.en: The noun admissio is recorded for 'a letting in, an approach'. The sense of acknowledging a fact is not classical Latin but developed later in French and English.
items.cn: 名词 admissio 有「放行、进入」的记录；而「承认某事实」的义项并非古典拉丁语所有，是后来在法语和英语中发展出来的。

items.en: Old French admission carried the word into English with the sense of a letting in and of acceptance.
items.cn: 古法语 admission 把这个词带进英语，义为「放行」与「接纳」。

items.en: The noun is recorded in English from the fifteenth century, the acknowledgement sense appears in the sixteenth, and the fee sense is generally dated to the nineteenth. Exact dates are uncertain.
items.cn: 这个名词自十五世纪起见于英语，承认义在十六世纪出现，入场费义一般认为定于十九世纪；确切年代不确定。

note.en: The look-alike group is built on the Latin verb mittere 'to send'; the near-meaning group gathers other words for entering and for confessing, which split the two halves of admission between them.
note.cn: 形近组都建立在拉丁动词 mittere「送」之上；近义组收其他表示「进入」与「认罪」的词，它们分别承担了 admission 的两半意思。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning to let in or to accept that something is true.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词，义为「准许进入」或「承认某事为真」。

entries.definition: The right to enter a place, formed with the suffix -ance and common on official notices.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入权、进入」，由后缀 -ance 构成，常见于正式告示。

entries.definition: Allowed to be used as evidence or accepted as valid, formed with -ible.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可采纳的、可接受的」，由后缀 -ible 构成。

entries.definition: An official order to do something, or a payment for a sale; it shares mittere with admission but has a different prefix and a different sense.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「委托、佣金」；与 admission 同出 mittere，但前缀不同、意义也已分开。

entries.definition: The act of entering or the door through which you enter; physical and concrete, unlike the abstract permission in admission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入、入口」，指具体动作或具体的门，不像 admission 那样偏重抽象的许可。

entries.definition: The act of going in, or an item entered in a list or competition; broader and less institutional.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入、条目、参赛作品」，范围更宽，机构色彩更淡。

entries.definition: A statement admitting guilt, especially in religion or law; heavier and more moral than admission.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「供认、忏悔」，多用于宗教或法律，语气比 admission 更重，道德意味更强。

entries.definition: The act of registering as a student or member; it names the sign-up rather than the decision to accept.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「注册、入学人数」，指完成注册这一动作，而不是学校决定录取。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb mittere and the phrases admission actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁动词 mittere，以及 admission 实际出现的搭配。

normal.en: Mittere is 'to send', so admission is being sent in through a door.
normal.cn: mittere 是「送」，所以 admission 就是被送进门里去。

normal.en: Mission, permit, transmit and admit all carry the same mittere.
normal.cn: mission、permit、transmit 与 admit 都带着同一个 mittere。

normal.en: An admission fee is the price of the door, not the price of what is inside.
normal.cn: admission fee 是那道门的价钱，不是门里那些东西的价钱。

normal.en: Hospital staff speak of an admission when a patient is taken in and written on the ward list.
normal.cn: 病人被收进医院、名字写进病房名单时，医护人员说的就是一次 admission。

normal.en: An admission that something is true is a fact finally allowed past the guard.
normal.cn: admission that something is true 就是一个终于被放过大门的真相。

abstract.en: Picture one gate doing two jobs: it lets people into a building and it lets an unwelcome fact into a conversation.
abstract.cn: 想象同一道门兼做两件事：既放人进楼，也把一个不受欢迎的事实放进谈话里。

abstract.en: The noun always looks at the moment of passing through, never at what happens afterwards.
abstract.cn: 这个名词看的始终是「穿过门」的那一刻，而不是之后发生了什么。

abstract.en: A fee, a letter of acceptance and a confession are all tickets through the same opening.
abstract.cn: 一笔费用、一封录取通知和一次供认，都是穿过同一个出口的票。

examples.en: The museum charges no admission on public holidays.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆在公共假日不收门票。

examples.en: His admission of guilt ended the two-year dispute.
examples.cn: 他承认了自己的过错，这场持续两年的争执就此结束。

examples.en: Letters of admission will be mailed in March.
examples.cn: 录取通知书将在三月寄出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额的米神」——门口收银员说：想进去，先交我的米（钱）才神气：入场费、准入。

root: 拉丁语 admissio「放行、进入」，来自动词 admittere「放进来」，由 ad-「向」+ mittere「送」构成；mittere 同时是 mission、permit、transmit 的词根。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of admission is a single doorway seen from a different side: a fact let in, a price for passage, a right to enter, an academic gate, a hospital bed, or a statement admitted into the record.
sensesIntro.cn: admission 的每个义项都是同一道门的不同侧面：放一个事实进来、为通行定价、拥有进入的权利、跨过学业之门、被收进病床，或一份被记录接纳的陈述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gate that opens for people and for facts at the same time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道同时为人与事实打开的门。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a fact or a confession is let in past the guard of silence.
branches.cn: 记录线：一个事实或一份供认被放过了沉默这道岗。

branches.en: THE PRICE: the same passage is sold at the ticket window.
branches.cn: 价钱线：同一次通行在售票窗口被标上了价。

branches.en: THE RIGHT: the door grants or withholds the mere permission to pass.
branches.cn: 权利线：这道门只决定给不给通过的许可。

branches.en: THE SCHOOL: the academic gate, and the office that decides who passes it.
branches.cn: 学校线：学业之门，以及决定谁可以通过的那个部门。

branches.en: THE WARD: one building takes the image over, and the patient becomes a line on a list.
branches.cn: 病房线：某座建筑接过了这个意象，病人成了名单上的一行。

intro.en: Admission is a Latin action noun; its endings and the verb behind it still build admittance, admissible and inadmissible.
intro.cn: admission 是拉丁语动作名词；它的词尾以及背后的动词，至今仍在构成 admittance、admissible 与 inadmissible。

latinIntro.en: Latin mittere, admittere and admissio are all recorded, and admissus is the recorded past participle.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere、admittere 与 admissio 均有文献记录，admissus 是记录在案的过去分词。

items.exampleCN: 它标出朝里面移动的方向。

items.example: It is the shared root of mission and permit.

definition_en: to cut hair from the skin, to cut a thin piece off, to reduce a small amount, or the act of shaving
core_image: 剃刀贴着下巴滑下，留下一道干净的白痕
scene: 他每天早上刮胡子。 He shaves every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 shave 是「刮胡子」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他每天早上刮胡子。

senses.title: Cut hair
senses.definition: to cut hair from the face or body
senses.definitionCN: 把脸上或身上的毛剃掉
senses.example: He shaves every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他每天早上刮胡子。
senses.why: This is the everyday personal care sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常个人护理义项。

senses.title: Slice off
senses.definition: to cut a thin piece from a surface
senses.definitionCN: 从表面削下薄薄一片
senses.example: He shaved a thin slice of cheese.
senses.exampleCN: 他削下一薄片奶酪。
senses.why: The razor motion is applied to any thin slice.
senses.whyCN: 剃刀的动作被用于任何薄片。

senses.title: Reduce slightly
senses.definition: to reduce an amount by a small degree
senses.definitionCN: 小幅度减少数量
senses.example: They shaved ten percent off the price.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把价格削减了百分之十。
senses.why: A thin slice removed is a small reduction.
senses.whyCN: 削掉薄薄一层就是小幅减少。

senses.title: A close shave
senses.definition: a narrow escape from danger
senses.definitionCN: 从危险中勉强脱身
senses.example: That was a close shave.
senses.exampleCN: 那真是侥幸脱险。
senses.why: The phrase comes from passing very near the razor.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语来自险些被剃刀刮到。

intro.cn: shave 源自古英语 sceafan，意为刮或剃。

items.en: The root meant to scrape or cut.
items.cn: 这个词根意为刮或切。

items.en: Sceafan meant to scrape hair from skin.
items.cn: sceafan 意为从皮肤上刮去毛发。

items.en: A close shave became an idiom for near danger.

note.cn: 把 shave 与形近词以及表示切割和修整的词作比较。
