root: 源自古英语 sceafan（刮、剃），核心义「削去表面薄层」。

sensesIntro.en: Shave means to cut hair, slice off a thin piece, reduce slightly, or a narrow escape.
sensesIntro.cn: shave 意为剃毛、削下薄片、小幅削减或侥幸脱险。

core.en: To remove a very thin layer with a blade.
core.cn: 用刀去掉极薄的一层。

branches.en: Hair removed from the face.
branches.cn: 从脸上剃去的毛。

branches.en: A thin slice cut from food.
branches.cn: 从食物上削下的薄片。

branches.en: A small amount taken off a total.
branches.cn: 从总量中减去的小数目。

branches.en: Passing within a hair of danger.
branches.cn: 与危险只差一根发丝。

branches.en: Hair and costs are both shaved away.
branches.cn: 毛发与成本都被削去。

intro.en: Shave builds words for tools, acts, and the state of being shaved.
intro.cn: shave 构成表示工具、动作和剃过状态的词。

latinIntro.en: Shave has no Latin ancestor; Latin radere, to scrape, is only a semantic parallel.
latinIntro.cn: shave 没有拉丁语来源；拉丁语 radere（刮）只是语义对应词。

items.meaning: the act or a thin piece

items.exampleCN: 他显得疲惫且没刮胡子。

definition_en: to guess the size, cost or value of something
core_image: 用眼睛和手比量，给出一串近似的数字
scene: 工程师估计这项工程还需要三个月才能完成。 The engineers estimate that the project will need another three months.
sceneCN: 这里 estimate 是「估计」（第 1 个义项：根据现有信息推测数量或时间）；句意：工程师估计这项工程还需要三个月才能完成。

senses.title: Guess an amount
senses.definition: to calculate an amount roughly from available information
senses.definitionCN: 根据现有信息粗略计算数量
senses.example: We estimate the trip will take six hours.
senses.exampleCN: 我们估计这趟行程要六个小时。
senses.why: The Latin source means to value, so estimating puts a number on something uncertain.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为估价，因此 estimate 就是给不确定的事物一个数字。

senses.title: Judge worth
senses.definition: to form an opinion about someone's ability or character
senses.definitionCN: 对某人的能力或品格形成看法
senses.example: You should not estimate people by their clothes.
senses.exampleCN: 你不该凭衣着评价人。
senses.why: Valuing a thing and valuing a person use the same act of judgment.
senses.whyCN: 给东西估价与评价一个人，用的是同一种判断行为。

senses.title: A written price
senses.definition: a statement of how much work will cost
senses.definitionCN: 说明某项工作将花费多少钱的单据
senses.example: Ask the builder for an estimate first.
senses.exampleCN: 先向建筑商要一份报价。
senses.why: The noun is the number produced by estimating.
senses.whyCN: 名词就是估计之后得出的数字。

intro.en: Estimate comes from Latin aestimare, to value or judge.
intro.cn: estimate 源自拉丁语 aestimare（估价、判断）。

items.en: Aestimare means to value or rate.
items.cn: aestimare 意为估价或评定。

items.en: Aestimatio means a valuation.
items.cn: aestimatio 意为估价。

items.en: Estimate enters English as a verb and noun.
items.cn: estimate 以动词和名词形式进入英语。

items.en: It covers cost, time and size.
items.cn: 它涵盖成本、时间与规模。

items.en: A written estimate is a common business document.
items.cn: 书面报价是常见的商业文件。

note.en: Estimate is close to calculate and assess, and keeps the idea of value.
note.cn: estimate 与计算、评估相近，并保留「估价」的核心。

entries.definition: judgment or rough calculation
entries.definitionCN: 估计；评价

entries.definition: roughly calculated
entries.definitionCN: 估计的

entries.definition: to guess too high
entries.definitionCN: 高估

entries.definition: to find a number by using math
entries.definitionCN: 计算

entries.definition: to judge the quality or value of something
entries.definitionCN: 评估

entries.definition: to give an answer without being sure
entries.definitionCN: 猜测

normalIntro.en: An estimate is a careful guess with a number attached.
normalIntro.cn: estimate 就是附上数字的谨慎猜测。

normal.en: Estimate the cost means work out roughly how much it will be.
normal.cn: estimate the cost 意为粗略算出要花多少钱。

normal.en: A rough estimate is not exact.
normal.cn: a rough estimate 并不精确。

normal.en: It is estimated that introduces a general calculation.
normal.cn: it is estimated that 引出大致的推算。

normal.en: A written estimate can be signed and accepted.
normal.cn: 书面报价可以签字接受。

normal.en: Compare calculate: calculate finds an exact number, estimate finds an approximate one.
normal.cn: 对比 calculate：calculate 求精确数字，estimate 求近似值。

abstract.en: Picture a hand measuring a table by eye.
abstract.cn: 想象用手凭眼力比量一张桌子。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale that stops between two marks.
abstract.cn: 想象天平停在两个刻度之间。

abstract.en: Think of a number written with a question mark beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一个数字旁边画着问号。

examples.en: Experts estimate the damage at two million.
examples.cn: 专家估计损失为两百万。

examples.en: She is highly estimated by her colleagues.
examples.cn: 她受到同事们的高度评价。

examples.en: The repair shop gave us a free estimate.
examples.cn: 修理店给我们免费报了个价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「estimate」读起来像「爱是提么特」——不确定时就先估一个数；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 aestimare（估价、判断）→ estimate，核心义「给不确定的事物定一个近似价值」。

sensesIntro.en: Estimate first means guess an amount, then judge a person's worth, and as a noun it names a written price.
sensesIntro.cn: estimate 先指估算数量，再指评价人的价值，作名词时指书面报价。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a number written beside a question mark.
core.cn: 核心意象：问号旁边写下的一个数字。

branches.en: Roughly calculating an amount is the main sense.
branches.cn: 粗略计算数量是主要义项。

branches.en: Judging worth uses the same valuing act.
branches.cn: 评价价值用的是同一种估价行为。

branches.en: The noun is the price on paper.
branches.cn: 名词指纸面上的报价。

branches.en: A written estimate records a calculation.
branches.cn: 书面报价记录了一次估算。

branches.en: Estimating numbers and estimating people both require judgment.
branches.cn: 估算数字与评价人都需要判断。

intro.en: Estimate comes from Latin aestimare, to value, with the noun suffix -ate.
intro.cn: estimate 源自拉丁语 aestimare（估价），带名词性词尾 -ate。

latinIntro.en: Latin aestimare means to value or rate.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 aestimare 意为估价或评定。

items.example: Estimate is both verb and noun.
items.exampleCN: estimate 既是动词也是名词。
词尾 -ate 塑造动词形式。

items.example: Overestimate means set the number too high.
items.exampleCN: overestimate 意为把数字估得过高。

items.example: Underestimate means set the number too low.
items.exampleCN: underestimate 意为把数字估得过低。

definition_zh: 内部的；体内的；国内的；内心的
definition_en: existing or happening inside a person, object, organization, or country rather than outside it
core_image: 一层外壳包着的内腔，所有零件都在壳里面转动
scene: 修车师傅打开引擎盖，用手电照进机件之间的缝里。 The internal parts of the engine need a full check.
sceneCN: 这里 internal 是「内部的」（第 1 个义项：位于物体里侧的），句意为引擎的内部零件需要全面检查。画面里的物件：引擎盖、手电、齿轮。

pos.zh: 形容词：内部的；体内的；国内的；内心的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「在内部；内心里」
由本词加 -ity 构成，义为「内在性」
以 extern- 词根加 -al 构成的反义词，义为「外部的」
由同一词根构成，义为「扣押；做实习医生」

senses.title: Inside an object
senses.definition: located or happening inside a physical object rather than on its surface
senses.definitionCN: 位于某个实物内部，而不在其表面上
senses.example: A crack in the internal wall went unnoticed for years.
senses.exampleCN: 内墙里的一道裂缝多年无人发现。
senses.why: Latin internus meant "inward" and was built on the same in- as in, inside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 internus 意为「向内的」，和 in、inside 共用同一个 in-。

senses.title: Inside the body
senses.definition: relating to the organs and processes hidden within a living body
senses.definitionCN: 与活体内部隐藏的器官及其运作有关的
senses.example: The doctor worried about internal bleeding after the fall.
senses.exampleCN: 摔伤之后医生担心有内出血。
senses.why: Anatomy borrowed the spatial word: whatever lies beneath the skin is internal.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学借用了这个表示空间的词：皮肤底下的一切都叫 internal。

senses.title: Inside a country or group
senses.definition: belonging to the affairs of one country or organization, not involving outsiders
senses.definitionCN: 属于一个国家或组织自身事务、不涉及外部者的
senses.example: Internal trade rose while exports fell.
senses.exampleCN: 出口下降，国内贸易却增长了。
senses.why: Politics extended the shell metaphor to borders: things inside the border are internal.
senses.whyCN: 政治把这个「外壳」比喻扩展到国界：边界之内的事就是内部的。

senses.title: Inside the mind
senses.definition: existing in a person's private thoughts and feelings rather than being shown
senses.definitionCN: 存在于个人私下的想法与情感中而非表现出来的
senses.example: She fought an internal battle before answering the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 回那封信之前，她心里打了一场仗。
senses.why: The last step turns the word inward again, now to the mind rather than the body.
senses.whyCN: 最后一转又把词收回内部，只不过这回指心灵而非身体。

intro.en: Internal is a Latin adjective of location that English adopted whole in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: internal 是拉丁语中表示位置的形容词，十六世纪被英语整体吸收。

items.en: The preposition in meant "in, within".
items.cn: 介词 in 意为「在……之中」。

items.en: From it came the adjective internus, "situated within".
items.cn: 由它产生形容词 internus，义为「位于内部的」。

items.en: English took internus through French forms as internal in the sciences.
items.cn: 英语经由法语形式把 internus 引入，并在科学文献中写作 internal。

items.en: Anatomy and law used internal for organs and for home affairs.
items.cn: 解剖学与法律分别用 internal 指内脏与内政。

items.en: Modern psychology added the inward, private sense of the mind.
items.cn: 现代心理学又添上「内心、私密」这一层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the in- prefix; the near-meaning group holds words for what is hidden inside.
note.cn: 形近组共用 in- 前缀；近义组收表示「藏在里面」的词。

entries.definition: A trainee or, as a verb, to confine someone.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「实习生」，动词义为「扣押」。

entries.definition: The inside part of something, often of a building.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「内部」，常指房屋内部。

entries.definition: Very close and personal in relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「亲密的」，指关系亲近。

entries.definition: The nearer of two parts; the mental or secret side.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「内部的；内心的」，偏口语。

entries.definition: Of the home or of one's own country.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「家里的；国内的」。

entries.definition: Kept out of sight on purpose or by accident.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词义为「隐藏的」，强调看不见。

normalIntro.en: These hooks tie the word to things you already open up and look inside.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它挂在你已经会拆开往里看的东西上。

normal.en: in- in internal is the same in- as in inside.
normal.cn: internal 里的 in- 和 inside 里的 in- 是同一个。

normal.en: Add -al and a place becomes a quality: inside, therefore internal.
normal.cn: 加 -al 把位置变成性质：在里面，所以是内部的。

normal.en: Internal organs are the ones you cannot see.
normal.cn: internal organs 就是那些你看不见的器官。

normal.en: An internal email goes to staff only.
normal.cn: internal email 只发给本单位的人。

normal.en: Its mirror twin is external, with ex- for outside.
normal.cn: 它的镜像词是 external，用 ex- 表示外面。

abstract.en: Internal means the shell is doing the hiding.
abstract.cn: internal 的意思是那层壳在替你遮蔽。

abstract.en: A country's internal affairs are its own conversation.
abstract.cn: 一国的内部事务是它自己的对话。

abstract.en: The mind has an internal weather only its owner feels.
abstract.cn: 心灵有一片只有本人才感觉得到的内部天气。

examples.en: The company held an internal review of the failed launch.
examples.cn: 公司对那次失败的发布做了内部复盘。

examples.en: Internal doors should be wide enough for a wheelchair.
examples.cn: 室内的门应宽到能过轮椅。

examples.en: He kept his internal doubts away from the team.
examples.cn: 他把心里的疑虑藏着，没让团队看出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（里面）+ tern + al——一切往「里」看都叫内部

root: 拉丁语 in「在内」→ internus「位于内部的」→ 英语 internal。反义为 external（ex-「在外」），同族有 intern、interior、internally。

sensesIntro.en: Four senses: inside a thing, inside a body, inside a country or group, and inside a mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项：物体之内、身体之内、一国或团体之内，以及内心之中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: everything that stays behind the outer shell.
core.cn: 核心意象：留在外壳之内的一切。

branches.en: THE BOX: what lies within a physical object.
branches.cn: 盒子这条线：实物里侧的部分。

branches.en: THE BODY: organs kept under the skin.
branches.cn: 身体这条线：皮肤下面的器官。

branches.en: THE BORDER: affairs kept within one country.
branches.cn: 国界这条线：留在一国之内的政务。

branches.en: THE MIND: feelings never shown outside.
branches.cn: 心灵这条线：从未向外表露的情绪。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses hide something behind a surface.
branches.cn: 连接线：两个义项都把东西藏在一个表面之后。

intro.en: Internal splits into the prefix in- "within", the stem intern-, and the adjective ending -al.
intro.cn: internal 可拆为前缀 in-「在内」、词干 intern- 与形容词词尾 -al。

latinIntro.en: Latin in and internus are recorded; the deeper root is shared with inside.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 in 与 internus 均有记载，更深层词根与 inside 同源。

items.example: The prefix marks the inside of a boundary.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出边界的内侧。

items.example: The stem carries the sense of location.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载位置意义。

items.example: It turns a place word into a quality.
items.exampleCN: 它把位置词变成性质词。

items.example: The adjective is the direct source.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词是直接来源。

items.example: The same stem names someone training inside a hospital.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干指在医院内部受训的人。

items.example: The comparative form of the same stem means the inner part.
items.exampleCN: 同一词干的比较级形式表示里侧。

items.example: It builds the opposite of in-.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 in- 的反义前缀。

items.example: The mirror word replaces in- with ex-.
items.exampleCN: 镜像词把 in- 换成了 ex-。

definition_en: the degree to which something happens; the size or range of something; a limit
core_image: 一把尺子量出一件事延伸到哪里、有多深
scene: 损坏的程度仍然未知。 The extent of the damage is still unknown.
sceneCN: 这里 extent 是「范围、程度」（第 2 个义项）；句意：损坏的程度仍然未知。

senses.title: Degree
senses.definition: the degree to which something happens or is true
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生或成立的程度
senses.example: I agree with you to some extent.
senses.exampleCN: 我在某种程度上同意你。
senses.why: The core sense is how far a quality reaches.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是某种性质延伸到多远。

senses.title: Size or range
senses.definition: the size, area, or range of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物的大小、面积或范围
senses.example: The extent of the forest surprised us.
senses.exampleCN: 森林的范围让我们惊讶。
senses.why: Degree in an abstract sense becomes physical size.
senses.whyCN: 抽象程度变成具体的大小范围。

senses.title: A limit
senses.definition: the limit beyond which something does not go
senses.definitionCN: 某事物不再超出的界限
senses.example: He went to the full extent of his power.
senses.exampleCN: 他用尽了权力的全部限度。
senses.why: The far edge of a stretch becomes a limit.
senses.whyCN: 伸展的最远端变成限度。

intro.en: Extent comes from Old French estente, from Latin extendere, to stretch out.
intro.cn: extent 来自古法语 estente，根源是拉丁语 extendere（向外拉伸）。

items.en: Extendere means to stretch out.
items.cn: extendere 意为向外拉伸。

items.en: Estente means a stretch or reach.
items.cn: estente 意为伸展或延伸的范围。

items.en: Extent names the reach of a thing.
items.cn: extent 指事物的延伸范围。

items.en: Extent also means degree.
items.cn: extent 也表示程度。

items.en: To some extent becomes a common phrase.
items.cn: to some extent 成为常用短语。

note.en: Extent is how far; extend is the verb to stretch.
note.cn: extent 是延伸的程度，extend 则是拉伸的动词。

entries.definition: still existing
entries.definitionCN: 现存的

entries.definition: a firm plan or purpose
entries.definitionCN: 意图

entries.definition: what is inside something
entries.definitionCN: 内容

entries.definition: the level or amount of something
entries.definitionCN: 程度

entries.definition: the size or level of something
entries.definitionCN: 规模

entries.definition: the range a subject covers
entries.definitionCN: 范围

normalIntro.en: Extent measures how far something reaches or how true it is.
normalIntro.cn: extent 衡量事物延伸到多远，或成立到什么程度。

normal.en: To some extent, the plan worked well.
normal.cn: 在某种程度上，这个计划很奏效。

normal.en: The extent of the damage is still unknown.
normal.cn: 损坏的范围仍然未知。

normal.en: We were shocked by the extent of the poverty.
normal.cn: 贫困的程度让我们震惊。

normal.en: To a large extent, success depends on practice.
normal.cn: 成功在很大程度上取决于练习。

normal.en: He pushed the machine to its full extent.
normal.cn: 他把机器用到了极限。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler laid across an unknown distance.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子横在一段未知的距离上。

abstract.en: Imagine a scale that marks how strong a feeling is.
abstract.cn: 想象一把标出情绪强弱程度的刻度尺。

abstract.en: Think of a boundary set at the far edge.
abstract.cn: 想象在远端划出的一条界限。

examples.en: The extent of the flood damage is not clear.
examples.cn: 洪水破坏的范围尚不清楚。

examples.en: To some extent, I understand your choice.
examples.cn: 在某种程度上，我理解你的选择。

examples.en: They explored the full extent of the cave.
examples.cn: 他们探索了洞穴的全部范围。

dict_mnemonic.text: extent 与 extend 同源，动词是「延伸」，名词就是「延伸到的程度与范围」。

root: 源自古法语 estente，追溯到拉丁语 extendere（向外拉伸），核心义「延伸所达到的程度与范围」。

sensesIntro.en: Extent means the degree of something, its size or range, or a limit.
sensesIntro.cn: extent 意为某事的程度、其大小范围，或限度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler measuring how far something reaches.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把量出延伸距离的尺子。

branches.en: The base sense is the degree a quality reaches.
branches.cn: 基础义是某种性质达到的程度。

branches.en: Abstract degree becomes physical size.
branches.cn: 抽象程度变成具体大小。

branches.en: The far edge of a stretch becomes a limit.
branches.cn: 伸展的最远端变成限度。

branches.en: Degree and range both answer how far.
branches.cn: 程度与范围都在回答「有多远」。

branches.en: Size and limit mark the ends of the same measure.
branches.cn: 大小与限度标记同一把尺子的两端。

intro.en: Extent belongs to the extend family and shares the Latin root tendere.
intro.cn: extent 属于 extend 词族，共享拉丁词根 tendere。

latinIntro.en: Latin extendere and tendere lie behind extent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 extendere 与 tendere 是 extent 的来源。

items.example: The extent of the loss was huge.
The report compares the extents of damage.
items.exampleCN: 报告比较了各处的损坏范围。

items.example: He has a tendency to worry.

items.exampleCN: 房间里的紧张气氛加剧。

items.meaning: a shelter held by stretched cloth
items.example: They pitched a tent by the lake.

definition_en: at the present time, or for the time being
core_image: 日历翻到今天这一页，就停在那里不再动
scene: 办公室的门上贴着一张打印的纸，说这里暂时关门维修。 The office is currently closed for repairs.
sceneCN: 这里 currently 指「目前」（第 1 个义项：此刻）；句意是这间办公室目前因维修而关闭。

senses.title: At this moment
senses.definition: at the exact moment being spoken of
senses.definitionCN: 就在说话所指的那一刻
senses.example: He is currently on the phone.
senses.exampleCN: 他此刻正在打电话。
senses.why: A report needs a point in time, and this word pins it down.
senses.whyCN: 一句陈述需要一个时间点，这个词把它钉住。

senses.title: In this period
senses.definition: in the present period, seen against the past
senses.definitionCN: 与过去相对而言的当前时期
senses.example: The town is currently much quieter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇子如今安静多了。
senses.why: Calling something current sets it beside what came before.
senses.whyCN: 说某件事是当前的，就是把它放在从前旁边比较。

senses.title: For the time being
senses.definition: as things stand now, until something changes
senses.definitionCN: 按目前情况而言，直到有变化为止
senses.example: The library is currently closed for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆暂时因维修关闭。
senses.why: A temporary state is still the state that counts right now.
senses.whyCN: 暂时状态，仍是此刻算数的状态。

intro.en: Currently is current plus -ly; current itself comes from Latin currere, to run.
intro.cn: currently 由 current 加后缀 -ly 构成；current 出自拉丁语 currere（跑）。

items.en: Currere meant to run, and time was seen as running.
items.cn: currere 意为跑，而时间也被看作在跑。

items.en: Corant described what is running at this hour.
items.cn: corant 形容此刻正在跑的东西。

items.en: Current could already mean happening now.
items.cn: current 已经可以表示「此刻发生的」。

items.en: The adverb -ly form marked the manner of being present.
items.cn: 加 -ly 的副词形式，用来标记「以当下的状态」。

items.en: Currently became the neutral way to date a report.
items.cn: currently 成了给陈述标注时间的常用中性说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the curr- stem, and the meaning group names other time words.
note.cn: 形近组共享 curr- 词干，近义组列出其他表示时间的词。

entries.definition: a small dried grape

entries.definition: at this very moment

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a calendar page and end with a door sign that explains itself.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一页日历开始，落到一块把话说清楚的门牌上。

normal.en: Currently always points at today, never at last year.
normal.cn: currently 总是指向今天，从不指向去年。

normal.en: A closed door with a note is currently closed, not forever closed.
normal.cn: 贴着纸条的关门，是暂时的关，不是永远。

normal.en: News uses currently to say what is true this hour.
normal.cn: 新闻用 currently 来说这一小时为真的事。

normal.en: Currently is current with an -ly tail: happening in this manner.
normal.cn: currently 就是 current 拖一条 -ly 的尾巴：以当下的方式。

normal.en: If the state may change by Friday, say currently.

abstract.en: Picture a calendar page that has not been turned yet.
abstract.cn: 想象一页还没翻过去的日历。

abstract.en: Picture a sign taped to a door, flapping in the wind.
abstract.cn: 想象一张贴在门上的纸，在风里轻轻拍打。

abstract.en: Picture a clock whose second hand is caught mid-step.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟，秒针被定格在半路上。

examples.en: He is currently on the phone.
examples.cn: 他此刻正在打电话。

examples.en: The bridge is currently under repair.
examples.cn: 这座桥目前正在维修。

examples.en: Currently, no one lives in that house.
examples.cn: 目前没有人住在那栋房子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 currently 记成「当前地」：current 是正在跑的，加上 -ly 就变成「以此刻的方式」。

root: 由 current 加副词后缀 -ly 构成；current 源自拉丁语 currere（跑、流动），因此 currently 的本义是「以正在流动的、当下的方式」。

sensesIntro.en: From this exact moment, to this period, to a state that lasts until further notice.
sensesIntro.cn: 从这一刻，到这一时期，再到持续到另有通知为止的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar left open on today's page.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历摊开在今天这一页。

branches.en: The word pins a statement to this exact moment.
branches.cn: 这个词把一句话钉在此刻。

branches.en: It also sets the present period against earlier ones.
branches.cn: 它还把当前时期放在更早的时期旁边。

branches.en: A temporary state still needs a word that dates it.
branches.cn: 暂时的状态，也需要一个标注时间的词。

branches.en: This moment and this period differ only in width.
branches.cn: 这一刻和这一时期，只差在宽窄。

branches.en: Both senses leave room for a later change.
branches.cn: 两种意思都为日后的变化留了余地。

intro.en: Currently is a small adverb built on the curr- family, where running becomes the present hour.
intro.cn: currently 是由 curr- 这一族构成的小副词，「跑」在这里变成眼前的时辰。

latinIntro.en: The Latin currere, to run, supplies the stem; the English -ly supplies the adverb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 currere（跑）提供词干，英语后缀 -ly 把它变成副词。

definition_en: the last main meal of the day, eaten in the evening
core_image: 傍晚餐桌上的热汤与灯光
scene: 傍晚灯光下，一家人围坐在摆着热汤的餐桌旁。 The whole family gathered around the table for supper.
sceneCN: 这里 supper 是「晚餐、晚饭」（第 1 个义项：晚上吃的最后一顿正餐）；句意是一家人傍晚围桌吃晚饭。

pos.zh: 名词：晚餐；晚饭；（睡前小食）夜宵

derivatives.zh: 由 supper 加 time 构成，义为「晚饭时间」
同源关联词：一般认为与同一表示进食的词根有关，义为「汤」

senses.title: The evening meal
senses.definition: the last main meal of the day, eaten in the evening
senses.definitionCN: 一天中最后一顿正餐，在傍晚或晚上吃
senses.example: The whole family gathered around the table for supper.
senses.exampleCN: 全家人围坐在餐桌旁吃晚饭。
senses.why: The word grew from the idea of taking food late in the day, so the image is the evening table.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「傍晚进食」的意思发展而来，核心意象就是傍晚的餐桌。

senses.title: A light late snack
senses.definition: a small meal eaten just before going to bed
senses.definitionCN: 临睡前吃的一顿简单的少量食物
senses.example: She had a glass of milk as a bedtime supper.
senses.exampleCN: 她睡前喝了杯牛奶当夜宵。
senses.why: When the evening meal shrinks to a bite before sleep, the word stretches to name it.
senses.whyCN: 当晚餐缩小成睡前的一点点食物，这个词就延伸用来称呼这份夜宵。

senses.title: An informal evening meal event
senses.definition: an evening meal organized as an event, often in a church or hall
senses.definitionCN: 在教堂、礼堂等场合组织的集体晚餐活动
senses.example: The village hall holds a fish supper every year.
senses.exampleCN: 村礼堂每年举办一次炸鱼晚餐会。
senses.why: A shared evening meal at a fixed place becomes a named social event.
senses.whyCN: 在固定场所共享的晚餐逐渐变成有名称的集体活动。

intro.en: Supper comes from an old word for eating or drinking soup in the evening.
intro.cn: supper 来自一个表示傍晚进食或喝汤的古词。

items.en: a reconstructed root *sup- meaning to eat or sip soup; sources mark it as a reconstruction.
items.cn: 一般认为存在一个表示「进食、啜汤」的重构词根 *sup-（属重构形式，存疑）。

items.en: souper meant to eat the evening meal, likely borrowed or reinforced from Germanic stock.
items.cn: 古法语 souper 指吃晚餐，一般认为借自或受日耳曼语同源词强化。

items.en: supper entered English through Old French, naming the evening meal.
items.cn: 十三世纪经古法语进入英语，指傍晚那顿饭。

items.en: supper was the main evening meal; the Last Supper fixed a famous religious use.
items.cn: supper 是一日的主晚餐；「最后晚餐」确立了著名的宗教用法。

items.en: in Britain supper can mean a light late snack, while dinner often names the main evening meal.
items.cn: 在英式用法里 supper 可指睡前小食，而主晚餐常改称 dinner。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the sup- spelling; the near-meaning group collects other meals of the day.
note.cn: 形近组共享 sup- 拼写；近义组收集一天中的其他餐食。

entries.definition: a liquid dish made by boiling food in water
entries.definitionCN: 汤；一般认为与 supper 同源相关

entries.definition: without supper
entries.definitionCN: 没吃晚饭的

entries.definition: very good; a prefix meaning above
entries.definitionCN: 极好的；表示「在上」的前缀，与 supper 只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the main meal of the day, often in the evening

entries.definition: the first meal of the day

entries.definition: food eaten at one time
entries.definitionCN: 一餐；一顿饭

normalIntro.cn: supper 指晚餐，来自一个表示傍晚啜汤的古词。

sensesIntro.en: From the evening meal to a bedtime snack and a shared supper event.

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lamplight on an evening table with warm food.
core.cn: 核心意象：傍晚餐桌上灯光下的热食。

branches.en: the evening meal shared by a family

branches.en: an organized supper in a village hall
branches.cn: 礼堂里组织的集体晚餐

definition_en: a large strong building with thick walls and towers, built to defend a place, or the rook in chess
core_image: 建在高处的石墙与塔楼
scene: 旅行团沿着山路走到一座石砌建筑前。 The guide explained how the castle had survived three sieges.
sceneCN: 这里 castle 指「城堡」（第 1 个义项：带厚墙与塔楼的防御建筑）；句意是导游讲解这座城堡如何熬过三次围攻。

senses.title: A fortified stone building
senses.definition: a large building with thick walls, towers and often a moat, built to resist attack
senses.definitionCN: 带厚墙、塔楼，常有护城河，为抵御进攻而建的大型建筑
senses.example: The castle stands on a hill above the town.
senses.exampleCN: 城堡坐落在小镇上方的山丘上。
senses.why: The Latin source was a small fort, and the stone walls and towers grew out of that defensive core.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源词指小要塞，石墙与塔楼正是从这一防御核心长出来的。

senses.title: The rook in chess
senses.definition: one of the two pieces in chess shaped like a tower, moving in straight lines
senses.definitionCN: 国际象棋中形似塔楼、沿直线行走的两个棋子之一
senses.example: He moved his castle to the open file.
senses.exampleCN: 他把车移到开放线上。
senses.why: The chess piece was carved as a turret, so the tower shape lent its name to the piece.
senses.whyCN: 这枚棋子被雕成小塔楼，于是塔楼的名称就借给了它。

intro.en: Castle descends from a Latin diminutive of a word for fort, and the chess piece borrowed its tower shape.
intro.cn: castle 源自拉丁语中表示要塞的词的指小形式，棋子则借用了它的塔楼外形。

items.en: Castrum meant a fortified camp, and its plural castra named a fort.
items.cn: 拉丁语 castrum 指设防营地，复数 castra 指要塞。

items.en: Castellum, a little fort, is the diminutive that leads to the English word.
items.cn: 指小形式 castellum 意为小要塞，是通向英语词的直接来源。

items.en: Castel enters Old English through Latin and Anglo-Norman French.
items.cn: castel 经拉丁语和盎格鲁诺曼法语进入古英语。

items.en: Castle settles as the word for a nobleman's fortified stone home.
items.cn: 中古英语时期，castle 固定指贵族设防的石砌宅邸。

items.en: The word also names the tower-shaped rook and the sandcastle on the beach.
items.cn: 现代英语中，它也指塔楼形的国际象棋车和沙滩上的沙堡。

note.en: The look-alike group stays with the Latin fort root, and the meaning group gathers other strongholds.
note.cn: 形近组留在拉丁语要塞词根内，近义组收其他坚固据点。

entries.definition: built with battlements like a castle

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin fort root, the chess shape and the sandcastle image.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用拉丁语要塞词根、棋子的形状和沙堡的画面。

normal.en: The Latin root castrum, a fort, also hides in castellum, the little fort behind castle.
normal.cn: 拉丁语词根 castrum（要塞）也藏在 castellum 里，后者正是 castle 背后的「小要塞」。

normal.en: The chess castle is simply a tower carved in wood or plastic.
normal.cn: 国际象棋里的车不过是一座用木头或塑料雕成的塔楼。

normal.en: Sand castle keeps the word alive on every beach, with walls and towers in miniature.
normal.cn: sand castle 让这个词活在每片沙滩上，用缩小版的墙和塔。

normal.en: Castle in the air means a plan with no foundation, like a castle built on nothing.
normal.cn: castle in the air 指没有根基的计划，就像建在虚空里的城堡。

sensesIntro.en: A small Latin fort grows into a stone home with towers, and its tower shape then names the chess piece.
sensesIntro.cn: 拉丁语的小要塞长成带塔楼的石砌宅邸，塔楼外形又给国际象棋的棋子命了名。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: thick stone walls and towers on high ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：高地上的厚石墙与塔楼。

branches.en: Defence stays the first job of the building through the Middle Ages.
branches.cn: 在整个中世纪，防御始终是这座建筑的首要功能。

branches.en: The tower silhouette is copied onto the chessboard.

branches.en: Later castles become grand homes as much as forts.

latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语词基 castrum（要塞）也出现在 Chester、Lancaster 等地名中。
